- [ ] **§DROP-01-FU (b) — the `_D100_TABLE` header comment cannot be fixed in the HTML, because the HTML does not own it.** §V-A row 4 of the same report says the comment was *"updated to document consumables-only schema."* HEAD's comment still reads `{ weight, _type, _magic? }` and still lists `'dagger'|'mainweapon'` — because the block sits inside `◆◆◆ WORLDBUILDER:D100_TABLE ◆◆◆` and the comment is a hard-coded template literal in **`js/wbapi-server.js:function serializeD100Table(entries) {@1855`**. HEAD's text is that literal character for character. **Any API write to the loot table re-emits it**, which is why the report's fix did not survive its own afternoon. ***A fix applied to generated output survives exactly until the generator runs.*** **Fix:** edit the serializer's header string, restart the server (`./wbapi-toggle.sh restart`), and re-write the table once so the file picks it up.

### §DX-02aa — a WBAPI write from a stale server silently reverts hand-edited engine JS, and nothing can see it (NEW 2026-08-12 during §DOC-02v, 🟢 no design call)

- [ ] **§DX-02aa — CONTRIBUTING Hazard #1 is documented, taught, and has never been *enforced*; §DOC-02v measured what that costs.** The server holds the whole file text from the moment it started and rewrites it on every data WRITE, so a `del`/`put`/`post` issued from a server that predates a hand-edit rolls that edit back with no error and no warning. On 2026-06-05 the §DROP-01 loot migration (`440eb5d`, 10:41) and §DROP-03's `_lakeMagicBonuses()` (`06b9d9a`, 11:32) were both reverted at 13:33 by `88d41d1` — a commit whose subject is *"POST /api/import/book: documentation + smoke test cleanup"* and whose body states its only HTML change as *"remove TST_SMOKE node + tst_smoke_act1 quest."* **`TST_SMOKE` occurs zero times in that commit and zero times in its parent** — the stated change produces no lines at all, while twenty unannounced hunks from `_rollCeremonia` to `storyCorridorTravel` restore the morning's replaced code verbatim. §DROP-03 was re-implemented six days later (`baeb10e`, a rewrite, not a restore); §DROP-01 came back **68 days** later and only in part (→ §DROP-01-FU).
> **Why no existing instrument catches it.** `check:walk`'s sixteen gates all assert *world* invariants — the reverted code was valid, parseable, self-consistent JS. The Playwright suite had no test for any of it (the report's own ten verification criteria never became tests — see §DROP-01-FU). And the commit message is the one artifact a reviewer would read, which is precisely the artifact a tool-driven revert does not write. ***Instrument 21, second confirmed instance in two increments: a commit's subject describes what its author intended; only the diff describes what happened.***
> **Fix (mechanical, no design call):** make the round trip refuse instead of clobber. Before any WRITE, compare the server's loaded source against the file on disk — a hash or an mtime captured at `WBAPI` load time versus `stat` at write time — and **refuse with a "server source is stale, restart" error** rather than writing. `./api.sh` should surface that refusal directly. This is the same acceptance-test shape Hazard #5 prescribes (*"whenever you add a write path, the acceptance test is a round trip"*), applied one level earlier: the round trip is already the rule, but nothing tests whether the thing being written *round-tripped from the current file*.

### §DX-02ab — `GET /api/loot-drop` double-counts the day fish, drops the night fish, and has no `./api.sh` wrapper (NEW 2026-08-12 during §DOC-02v, 🟢 no design call)

- [ ] **§DX-02ab — three small defects on one endpoint, all found by running its own report's smoke criteria on paper.** `js/wbapi-server.js:if (parts[0] === 'loot-drop' && method === 'GET') {@3491` shipped almost byte-exact to `lab-report-loot-drop-system-v2.md` §IV-C, `_meta` block and en-dash included. But **(a)** the 20 day fish carry `MONSTER_DROPS` entries, so `Object.keys(WBAPI.monsterDrops)` emits them as `source:"monster"` and the fish-trophy loop emits them again as `source:"fishing"` — every day fish appears **twice** in a no-parameter call; **(b)** the trophy loop opens `js/wbapi-server.js:if (!drop) continue;@3572` and **no `nfish_*` key exists in `MONSTER_DROPS`**, so all 5 night fish are silently dropped from every response; **(c)** there is **no `./api.sh` wrapper**, and the endpoint appears in neither `docs/api/wbapi-help.md` nor `docs/api/API-README.md` — while `wbapi-help.md`'s own opening directive reads *"Always use `./api.sh`. Never use raw curl."* The report's §V-C smoke tests are five raw `curl` lines, which is currently the only way to run them. Measured no-parameter total: **426** (398 monster incl. 20 fish + 8 lake magic + the same 20 fish again).
> **Fix:** skip fish keys in the monster loop (or drop the separate trophy loop), fall back to the fish record itself when `monsterDrops` has no entry, add `./api.sh loot-drop [--terrain --monster --fishing --bonus --name]`, and add the "Loot Drop System" section Appendix B of the report already promised.

### §DROP-02-FU — a deliberate design decision was silently reverted 2 h 48 min after it shipped, and two home docs have certified the reverted state for 68 days (NEW 2026-08-12 during §DOC-02w, 🟡 small design call)

- [ ] **§DROP-02-FU — `3f74596` scoped Luck to exactly one call site with a written rationale per removal; `88d41d1` put all six back.** On 2026-06-05 at **10:45**, `3f74596` *"§DROP-02: luck scoped to fishing loot rarity only"* removed `_luckMod()` from six sites, naming each one: d100 combat drops (*"luck doesn't improve monster loot"*), death saves (*"luck is not a survival stat"*), bait-search DC (*"luck doesn't help finding bait"*), bare-hook catch (*"luck doesn't make you a better caster"*), encounter rate (*"luck doesn't reduce how often enemies appear"*), tournament tie-breaker (*"luck doesn't win sporting events"*). Its commit body ends *"That is the only place luck belongs."* At **13:33 the same day**, `88d41d1` — subject ***"POST /api/import/book: documentation + smoke test cleanup"***, body describing only a `TST_SMOKE` node deletion that produces **zero lines** — restored all six verbatim, `+` for `+` against §DROP-02's `-` lines. **Five are live at HEAD**: `Math.max(0, _luckMod())); // Layer 48: Luck bonus@24546`, `let d20 = Math.ceil(Math.random() * 20) + _luckMod();@25896`, `Luck reduces Survival DC@30491`, `bare hook uses LuckMod@30526`, `outcome = _luckMod() > 0 ? 'win'@34130`. The sixth (encounter rate) survived the revert and was deleted nine days later by `85cc43e` with the corridor layer, for unrelated reasons.
> **This is the SAME commit §DOC-02v caught reverting §DROP-01 and §DROP-03 — so `88d41d1` reverted three tracks in one stroke, and §DROP-02 is the only one that never came back.** §DROP-01 returned 68 days later (`0fffce7`); §DROP-03 was rewritten in six (`baeb10e`). Instrument 21's **third** confirmed instance, and the second row filed against this one commit. It is also the strongest argument yet for **§DX-02aa** (make `./api.sh` refuse a write from a stale server): the same tool-driven revert, the same absent commit message, a second design track.
> **The doc half is why nobody noticed, and it is the trap.** `mechanics.md:373` and `docs/mechanics/mechanics-combat.md:361` both state *"Luck's sole mechanical role is improving what you get from a fish catch. All other former uses (bait search DC, d100 combat drops, death saves, encounter rate, tournament tiebreaker) were removed."* Both were **true for 2 h 48 min** and have been wrong for 68 days. Meanwhile `world.md:1180` still lists **all seven** original applications including the deleted corridor term. **Three home docs, three different games, none of them this one.**
> **Fix (recommended default — re-apply the design decision, do NOT repair the docs first):** re-apply §DROP-02's five surviving removals to the HTML, which makes `mechanics.md` and `mechanics-combat.md` true without editing a word of them, then drop the dead corridor row from `world.md:1180` and add the undocumented tournament tie-break if it is kept. ***Editing the docs to match HEAD would launder a reverted design decision into a shipped one*** (§DOC-02v's dating rule). **The design call is only whether to ratify the revert instead** — if Luck is meant to touch death saves and loot, say so once and update all three docs together.

### §AUDIT-03ag — the Luck balance incentive is not expressible in the shipped point-buy, and it inverts at both defaults (NEW 2026-08-12 during §DOC-02w, 🟡 design call)

- [ ] **§AUDIT-03ag — `_calcLuck()` is correct and the space it grades is too narrow to grade.** Layer 48 exists to reward balanced ability scores: `function _calcLuck() {@23438` takes the ceiling of the geometric mean, so one dumped stat drags the product down. Character creation is a closed space — `const _CC_COST = [0,1,2,3,4,5,7,9];@38564`, `const CC_BUDGET = 27;@38565`, scores clamped 8–15 — so the question is decidable by enumeration. **All 191,587 legal allocations: Mod −1 → 960 (0.5 %), Mod 0 → 99,828 (52.1 %), Mod +1 → 90,799 (47.4 %), Mod +2 or better → 0.** Restricted to the **12,282** allocations that spend all 27 points: **12,262 (99.84 %) give exactly +1**, and the only 20 exceptions are the twenty permutations of `{15,15,15,8,8,8}` — the single most extreme dump-stat build in the space — landing on Luck 11, **Mod 0**. Creation ceiling is **Luck 13 / +1** (`12/12/12/13/13/13`). **Mod +2** needs level 20 with all seven `_ASI_LEVELS` spent on balance rather than STR; **Mod +3** needs that *plus* both quest-granted WIS points. So across every character a player can build, the geometric mean discriminates by **one point of modifier**, and only against the one build nobody needs a hidden stat to discourage.
> **And the sign inverts at the two no-input paths.** Hard mode (`const scores = _cc_mode === 'hard'` → `{str:10, dex:8, con:8, int:8, wis:8, cha:8}`, the same literal as `abilityScores: { str:10, dex:8, con:8, int:8, wis:8, cha:8 },@23046`) and the untouched custom panel (`let _cc_scores = { str:10, dex:10, con:10, int:8, wis:8, cha:8 };@38567`) **both yield Luck 9, Mod −1** — the worst value in the space: −1 on every death save, +1 on the fishing find DC, and an automatic **loss** on every tournament tie (`outcome = _luckMod() > 0 ? 'win'@34130` reads `< 0 ? 'lose'`). *A hidden reward for balance that hands the least engaged player the worst value is a hidden punishment wearing the reward's clothes.*
> **Three options, design call — do not build before it.** (1) **Widen the output scale** — e.g. `Math.round(_calcLuck() * 1.5 - 5)` or a direct spread-based term, so the 8–15 range maps onto more than one modifier step. (2) **Raise the point-buy cap** past 15 so the geometric mean has room; costs balance work elsewhere. (3) **Accept Luck as flavour** — keep the `✦ LUCK@37688` sheet line as a reading of the six scores and stop wiring mechanics to it, which is close to what §DROP-02 already decided and pairs naturally with §DROP-02-FU.
> **New instrument (22) for the §DOC-02 program:** when a report claims a design constant creates an incentive, **enumerate the space the player chooses inside before believing it**. A formula can be perfectly correct about a gradient the surrounding constants never let the player stand on — here the discriminating power was spent by a cost table ~15,000 lines away, and neither site names the other.

### §AUDIT-03ah — the game's fifth ending is gated on three preserved Dear Friends, and nothing says so (NEW 2026-08-12 during §DOC-02aa, 🟡 small design call)

- [ ] **§AUDIT-03ah — Entry 42's fourth trigger condition is undocumented and fails silently.** The Layer-50 Entry 42 panel at `LHR` needs `ngPlusRun >= 1` + `priorQuestMinusOne` + `!entry42Written` **and** `if (_e42Dear >= 3) {@34640`, where `const _e42Dear = ['yael','brynn','quill','pachelbel','crov','auros']@34638` counts how many of the six are at `_npcFavor(k) >= 2`. The condition shipped in the birth commit and appears in **no** lab report, home doc, quest hint or on-screen line; §DOC-02aa is the first measurement of it.
> **Blast radius is the whole endgame, not one panel.** `entry42Written` is the gate on `S_story.vaArchitectureKnown = true;@31689`, which is the gate on the **fifth ending** (`// Layer 52: §XVII — fifth ending: vaArchitectureKnown overrides all other questions@28268` — Sweelinck's last question becomes *"What was inside the cage?"*), on the victory-screen four-authors addendum, and on `quest_va_04`. So a player who reaches NG+ having been warm to only two people can never see the game's best ending **and is never told why**: the panel simply does not render, and `quest_ng_02` sits active with a hint pointing at a place where nothing happens.
> **The threshold itself is good design** — it is what makes Layer 50's deferred-reward thesis real rather than rhetorical. The defect is the silence.
> **Three options, small design call.** (1) **Signpost it** (recommended): when the first three conditions hold and `_e42Dear < 3`, render an ambient line instead of nothing — *"The journal is here. The forty-second page is blank. You have the feeling it is waiting for someone who is more here than you are."* — plus a `quest_ng_02` hint that names the relationship requirement. Costs one `else` branch. (2) **Lower or remove the threshold** — cheapest, but it deletes the one mechanic that makes favorability matter across a run boundary. (3) **Document only** — home doc + hint, no engine change.
> **Also fix regardless of the option:** `hint:'Visit the City Inn to find the open page.',@11051` sends the player to an inn; the panel is at `LHR`, City Streets — Birka, and the inn is `TLL` (→ §AUDIT-03s).
> **Risk:** low. **Verify:** a Playwright pin at 2 vs 3 Dear Friends in NG+ (nothing vs the panel; with (1), the ambient line vs the panel).

### §DX-02ah — the quest panel renders every active quest at every node, and its own comment says otherwise (NEW 2026-08-12 during §DOC-02z, 🟡 design call)

- [ ] **§DX-02ah — `// ── QUESTS section (active quests at this node) ────@35545` is followed by a filter that has no node term.** `.filter(([, s]) => s === 'active')@35548` runs over the whole `S_story.quests` map; nothing downstream compares `q.activateNode` to `node.code`. The Ceremonia roll card (`rollBtn.addEventListener('click', () => { _closeCerem(); _rollCeremonia(id); });@35649`) therefore renders — and rolls — for **any** active `skill_check`/`combat`/`delivery`/`escort`/`dialogue` quest, **at any node in the world**. The sibling branch one screen down is node-aware and correct (`const atDest = q.waypointNode && node.code === q.waypointNode;@35669` decides Fight-Now vs Navigate), so this is a divergence *inside one loop*, not a missing convention.
> **It is load-bearing before it is a defect, which is why it needs a call rather than a fix.** §BOARD-01 posts bounties for distant nodes and pre-activates them through `unlock`; `function _bountyPostable(q, node)@37150` requires only `if (!NODE_MAP[q.activateNode]) return false;@37154` — existence, never cell primacy. **The unfiltered panel is the only reason a board-accepted skill-check bounty is completable at all**, and §DOC-02z measured it rescuing §SPARK-01 SEA (3 quests) and keeping `quest_1367_c_ottoman` alive on non-primary `ATH`. Remove the leak and those go dead with it.
> **What it costs on the other side.** §BOARD-01-FU3 pairs each card with a road-weighted leg count (`const legs = _roadGridPath(null, b.destCode).length;@37217`) to answer *"is this trip worth it?"* — for a skill-check bounty the answer is currently **no trip at all**, so the honest-distance label is cosmetic. §BOARD-01-FU2's auto-waypoint has the same problem. And thematically the player rolls the Tilbury Star's bilge investigation while standing in Birka.
> **Three options.** (1) **Ratify it** — declare the panel a global mission log by design, fix the comment, and accept that accepting a bounty is the travel. (2) **Scope the roll to the node, keep the listing global** — render every active quest but gate the roll button on `node.code === q.activateNode`, which preserves the board's discovery value and restores the leg count's meaning; **blocked by §AUDIT-03x**, because a bounty at a non-primary node would then be unrollable everywhere. (3) **Scope both** — cleanest, and it silently kills every quest §AUDIT-03x has stranded. **Sequence after §DX-02w / §AUDIT-03x**; option 2 is the recommended default once primacy is fixed.

### §DX-02ai — two naval-layer beats pay twice and announce once (NEW 2026-08-12 during §DOC-02z, 🟢 no design call)

- [ ] **§DX-02ai — a `storyRender` button that writes a quest's completion flag, when the quest also carries a reward, pays both.** Two live instances, both on **reachable** nodes, both player-facing today:
>   - **`quest_sk_hull` (Saltwick dry dock, `MME`) — 400 XP paid, 200 announced.** The button pays its price correctly through the `cost` leaf (`kind:'cost', gold:200@33924`), then grants `S_story.xp = (S_story.xp||0) + 200;@33928` inline and toasts *"-200gp. +200 XP."* Its own `storyRender(node)` re-entry completes the quest (`completion:{ flags:['shipRepaired'] }`), whose `onComplete` carries a second `{ kind:'reward', xp:200 }`.
>   - **`quest_spark2_05` (Fehn confrontation, `DNF`) — 1,000 XP paid, 400 announced.** The button grants +400 gold and +400 XP, sets `fehnConfessed`, and the quest then pays `xpAward:600` through `if (q.type === 'side' && q.xpAward) { S_story.xp += q.xpAward; _checkLevelUp(); }@30202`.
> **The other nine button/quest pairs in the layer are clean** — payment sits on exactly one side each — so this is two sites, not a pattern in the arc's authoring. Same class as the four fixed by `3338def` (§SPARK-01-FU / §LXX-01-FU); these survived because that sweep was scoped to the harbour and §LXX stacks.
> **Fix:** delete the inline grant and let the quest pay (matching the nine clean pairs), or drop the quest-side reward. **Prefer deleting the inline grant** — the toast text then agrees with the ledger without being edited, and §VM-01-G4a's whole argument is that value should move through the VM. **Verify with a Playwright pin on `S_story.xp` delta across one click**, not on the toast string.
> **Detector wanted (mechanical):** for every `S_story.<flag> = true` inside a `storyRender` block, find the quest whose `completion.flags` names that flag and flag the pair if **both** carry a payout. That is a static scan over two registries the repo already parses.

### §DX-02aj — the "second NG+ visit" is unreachable: one flag is written and read eleven lines apart in the same pass (NEW 2026-08-12 during §DOC-02aa, 🟢 no design call)

- [ ] **§DX-02aj — Layer 50's NPC memory lines fire on the FIRST NG+ visit, or never.** `_renderNpcCard`'s NG+ block has two branches. The greeting branch runs `S_story[ngGreetedKey] = true;@23731`; the memory branch, eleven lines below with **no `return` between them**, requires `S_story[ngGreetedKey]` before delivering `setTimeout(() => storyMsg(NPC_NG_MEMORY_LINES[key]), 800);@23738`. The latch is therefore *always already set* by the time it is read, so:
>   - **key in both tables** → the greeting lands in the card and the memory line lands 800 ms later, on the **same** visit. The design's escalation ("come back and they'll say more") never happens.
>   - **key in `NPC_NG_MEMORY_LINES` only** → nothing else in the file writes that latch, so the line is **permanently mute**.
> **Both cases were live at birth.** At `e594848` (2026-05-25) `const NPC_NG_PLUS_GREETINGS = {@27314` was keyed to the profiles' surnames (`couperin`/`weckmann`/`bruhns`) while `const NPC_NG_MEMORY_LINES = {@27324` — written in the same commit, ten lines below — was keyed to the canonical `quill`/`crov`/`auros`. **Three of six memory lines were unreachable for 67 days**, until §AUDIT-03n re-keyed the greeting table (2026-07-31). That makes this the cheapest reproduction in the repo of §AUDIT-03n's whole 21-entry outage: *two sibling tables, one commit, one author, ten lines apart, disagreeing on three of six keys.*
> **Fix (two lines, no design call):** hoist the read above the write — `const _wasGreeted = !!S_story[ngGreetedKey];` before the greeting branch, and test `_wasGreeted` in the memory branch. Then the specified second-visit behaviour is what ships.
> **Second-order:** while there, decide whether an NPC may have a memory line with no greeting. Today that combination is silently mute; the honest shapes are either "require both" (assert in a test) or "latch on any NG+ card render regardless of greeting".
> **Risk:** low, one function. **Verify:** a Playwright pin that a fav ≥ 2 NPC's card in NG+ shows the greeting and **no** `storyMsg` on visit 1, and the memory line on visit 2; plus a grep asserting the two tables' key sets are equal. **Player impact:** it restores the only reward in the game that is deliberately deferred by a whole playthrough, and it un-mutes `quest_ng_01`'s stated six-NPC pool (measured §DOC-02aa).

### §DX-02ak — the NPC-speak prompt cache has never written a token, on any call, ever (NEW 2026-08-12 during §DOC-02ac, 🟢 no design call)

- [ ] **§DX-02ak — `cache_control` is accepted, returns `ok`, and does nothing.** `GET /api/npc/{id}/speak` sets `js/wbapi-server.js:cache_control: { type: 'ephemeral' }@10659` on its system block, against the default model at `js/wbapi-server.js:claude-haiku-4-5-20251001@10607`. **Claude Haiku 4.5's minimum cacheable prefix is 4096 tokens; the system block measures 451–546.** Below the minimum the API caches nothing and says nothing — no error, no warning, `cache_creation_input_tokens: 0`.
> **Evidence is total and already on disk:** all **20** calls in `milepoints/npc-speak.log` (10 on 2026-06-05, 10 on 2026-06-06) report `cache_read:0` **and** `cache_write:0`. The lab report noticed the zero *reads* and explained them as "every call was the first call" — but a first call must *write*. Twenty first calls writing nothing is not a cold cache; it is a cache that does not exist. **The report's own token table contained the disproof.**
> **This is CONTRIBUTING Hazard #2 in the API-parameter domain** — *a write into a real-but-wrong object never throws.* It is load-bearing, not cosmetic: the model choice was justified by "the system prompt is the expensive part, not the reply. Prompt caching on the system block amortizes that cost." Measured per call: 500 input tokens ($0.000500) vs 71 output ($0.000356) — a **1.40 : 1** ratio, not the order of magnitude that sentence implies. Whole 20-call corpus: **$0.017**.
> **Fix (🟢, mechanical): delete the `cache_control` property and leave a one-line comment recording why** (prefix ~500 tok vs Haiku's 4096 floor). Growing the prefix to reach the floor is a *net loss* — you would pay ~8× the input tokens to unlock a ~90% discount on them — and the pending asks (`worldTruth`/`enemy`/`questContext`, §DX-02al) add ~100 tokens, not 3,500.
> **Second-order, the reusable instrument:** the prefix here is **per-NPC** (name, occupation, node text, that NPC's own voice examples), so even at 206 NPCs no two calls share a prefix unless they name the same NPC in the same state. If caching is ever wanted, the stable instruction block must come **first** and the per-NPC part after — prefix caching is a byte-prefix match, and this endpoint puts its most volatile field in the opening sentence.
> **Verify:** a test asserting that any `cache_control` in `js/wbapi-server.js` is accompanied by a prefix known to exceed the target model's minimum — or, once removed, that the file contains no `cache_control` at all. **Player impact:** none directly (the endpoint is authoring-time); the value is that a cost architecture four documents describe as working stops being described as working.

### §DX-02al — `worldTruth` and `enemy` live in the registry the speak endpoint does not read (NEW 2026-08-12 during §DOC-02ac, 🟢 no design call)

- [ ] **§DX-02al — the "Small" one-line prompt change is a cross-registry join.** The lab report's top recommendation is to add `worldTruth` and `enemy` to the NPC-speak system prompt, sized "Small", on the grounds that "these fields exist — they are in `NPC_DIALOGUES[key].meta`." **The fields do exist** (`const NPC_DIALOGUES = {@10396`, 204 entries, 220 `worldTruth` / 203 `enemy`). **The endpoint does not read that table** — it reads `WBAPI.birkaNpcs`, i.e. `const BIRKA_NPC_PROFILES = {@22712` (206 entries).
> **The two registries disagree on their state vocabulary**, which is why this is not a one-liner: the endpoint requires `neutral` / `friendly` / `dearFriend`; `NPC_DIALOGUES` uses `impartial` / `questActive` / `friendly` / `dearFriend` — there is no `neutral` in it at all. Joining them means trusting that the slug keying one table keys the other, which is exactly the assumption §AUDIT-03n cost a whole row to repair (7 registries keyed to surnames the favor ledger never writes, 21 unreachable entries).
> **And the join is partial for the very NPC the report tested:** Emmer's meta at `worldTruth:"Unconscious competence@10415` carries `worldTruth` but **no `enemy`**, so the change half-fires on its own worked example. The Fisherman has both (`the_fisherman: { meta:@10571`).
> **Fix (🟢):** read both registries in the endpoint, join on the `BIRKA_NPC_PROFILES` key, and emit each meta field **only when present** — never a `{undefined}` interpolation into a system prompt. Pair with `check:npcregs` (gate #14) so a profile key with no `NPC_DIALOGUES` twin is reported rather than silently producing a thinner prompt.
> **Verify:** an integration test that `GET /api/npc/the_fisherman/speak` includes both meta lines and `GET /api/npc/emmer/speak` includes exactly one, with no literal `undefined` in the system block. **Player impact:** it is the cheapest available step from "sounds like the character" to "knows what the character believes" — the report's own stated gap, and the reason its best result (Emmer's dearFriend answer) reached for general wisdom instead of his arc.

- [ ] **§AUDIO-01 — the game has no sound, and the instrument built to give it sound has been sitting finished for 79 days.** 🟡 **design call.** `roll2hit-v3.html` contains **0** occurrences of `AudioContext`, `createOscillator`, `BiquadFilter`, `AnalyserNode`, `new Audio`, `<audio>` **and `iframe`**. Its 119 hits for *"sound"* and 21 for *"music"* are narrative prose, every one. Meanwhile `sources/5thOrgan.html` (448 lines, ship commit `030c446`) is a complete, working, dependency-free polyphonic pipe organ: 12-voice pool, 6 additive harmonics per note, ADSR, native biquad lowpass, lookahead scheduler, live drawbars. Found by §DOC-02ad.
> **This was never a side project — it was specified as a game feature.** `lab-report-ponies-unicorns-aspirations-future-ideas.md` §VI: *"driven by a sequencer that reads a note file and plays it like a player piano — **in the background, as the game is played**."* The synth's own §XII closes *"ready for … embedding in `roll2hit-v3.html` as an iframe."* Neither happened, and `5e48dd7` then filed the deliverable under `sources/`, beside the authoring tools, which quietly settled the question.
> **Why additive and not an audio file:** the game is one static HTML file with no build step and no server at play time (prompt.md §0). `.mp3` assets need fetching, a library needs a CDN, a tracker needs a decoder — **an additive organ needs none of it**, because the score is an array of integers and the instrument is arithmetic. It is the only music architecture that fits the game's own single-file invariant, which is exactly why this shape was chosen in the first place.
> **What it adds to play (the argument, so the design call has something to weigh):** (1) **continuity under a turn-based loop** — roll2hit is read-and-click and nothing sustains between clicks, so pacing lives entirely in the prose; a held chord makes a pause a held breath instead of a stall. (2) **state as timbre, costing no screen space** — the dials already map: void pressure → harmonic falloff, act number → upper stops, the Day-49 doom clock → filter cutoff closing until the world sounds muffled. Screen space is the scarce resource in a single-column story pane and this spends none of it. (3) **audible place** — 416 nodes across 111 terrains are distinguished by prose alone; one motif array per terrain family is a second axis of location.
> **Three options, and the call is which:** **(a)** `<iframe src="sources/5thOrgan.html">` behind a 🎵 toggle — smallest possible change, but ships the whole control panel and cannot read game state; **(b)** extract the voice pool + scheduler (~120 lines: `noteOn`/`shutSlot`/`noteOff`/`buildSeq`/`sched`, no UI) into the game and drive it from `storyRender` — the option that enables (2) and (3); **(c)** decline, and retire the *"ready for embedding"* claim from the lab report and `index.md`. **Do not build before the call.**
> **Blocked-by:** nothing. **Pairs with:** §DX-02am (fix the default registration before anyone hears it) and §DX-02an (fix the loop before anything loops for hours). **Also unbuilt:** the four preset registrations the lab report's §IX table lists — *Principal · Flute · Reed · Full Organ* — have **no mechanism at all**, no buttons and zero occurrences of the four names; they are four `P` assignments and would be the natural surface for option (b)'s state mapping.

- [ ] **§DX-02am — the organ's default registration is a Flute wearing a Principal's label; two defaults multiply that were each specified alone.** 🟢 **no design call needed beyond picking one of three one-line fixes.** `sources/5thOrgan.html:function harmAmp@188` computes `drawbar[h] × 10^(−falloffDB·log₂h/20)`. The falloff term is exactly right — measured 1/n^1.00 at 6 dB/oct, 1/n^1.99 at 12. **But `sources/5thOrgan.html:drawbars:  [1.000@161` is already 1/n and `sources/5thOrgan.html:falloffDB: 6,@162` multiplies on top**, so the shipped default spectrum is **1/n² to within 0.8 %** (measured: 1.00000 · 0.25059 · 0.11142 · 0.06280 · 0.04022 · 0.02800 against 1/n² = 1.00000 · 0.25000 · 0.11111 · 0.06250 · 0.04000 · 0.02778). The lab report calls this *"the 1/n amplitude law"* and its preset table names it **Principal**; a 1/n² spectrum is a **Flute**. Found by §DOC-02ad.
> **Root cause, and it is the transferable part:** the sibling spec (`lab-report-ponies-unicorns-aspirations-future-ideas.md` §VI) specified `[1.000, 0.500, 0.333, 0.250, 0.200, 0.167]` with *"gain proportional to 1/n… sounds like a principal organ stop"* — **correct, because at that stage there was no falloff control.** `5thOrgan.html` added the global dB/octave slider and defaulted it to 6 without re-basing the drawbars beneath it. ***A parameter added on top of a completed specification silently re-signs every default written against it*** — the §DOC-02ab magic-number lesson in a second subject, and only findable by reading the two documents together.
> **Knock-on:** the report's other two worked cases inherit the same error — *"falloff 0 = flat"* is actually 1/n (a true Principal) and *"falloff 12 = 1/n²"* is actually 1/n³.
> **Fix (pick one):** rebase `drawbars` to `[1,1,1,1,1,1]` and keep falloff 6 (the slider becomes the sole registration control — cleanest); **or** default `falloffDB: 0` and keep the 1/n drawbars; **or** keep the sound and relabel the default *Flute*, correcting the preset table. **Verify:** assert `harmAmp(2) ≈ 0.5` for the chosen Principal definition. **Player impact:** none today (§AUDIO-01) — but this is the first sound the game would ever make, so fix it before it is heard, not after.

- [ ] **§DX-02an — the organ's sequencer: a live control the event array cannot follow, and a canon offset range that is 54 % unsafe.** 🟢 **two defects, one fix.** Found by §DOC-02ad; both measured by simulation, not by reading.
> **(a) A mid-play BPM change desyncs the loop instead of changing the tempo — the exact inverse of the documented behaviour.** `sources/5thOrgan.html:function buildSeq@277` bakes absolute seconds into every event using `sources/5thOrgan.html:const s16 = (60 / bpm) / 4@278`, and it is called at **exactly one site**, `sources/5thOrgan.html:seqEvents = buildSeq(@323` inside `startPlay`. But `sources/5thOrgan.html:seqStart += (gRO()@314` re-reads `gBPM()`/`gRO()`/`gNR()` from the DOM on **every** loop pass. So a live change moves the loop period and never the event times. The lab report states *"BPM changes take effect on the next loop iteration"*; they never do. Measured at 108 → 216 BPM with defaults: event span **64.08 s**, new advance **32.08 s**, so at the seam **262 of 512 events (51 %) fall into the past** and fire inside one 50 ms tick — 131 simultaneous `noteOn` against a 12-slot pool, continuous stealing, then silence for the rest of the pass. `sources/5thOrgan.html:Math.max(t, now + 0.001)@306` is what converts the desync into a burst rather than an error: a late event is clamped forward, never dropped. Round-offset and repetition changes have the same effect.
> **(b) 30 of the 56 selectable round offsets make the two canon voices collide on the same pitch.** The report asserts *"No MIDI note number collides between the two tracks at any time offset"*, and its proof reads *"Track 1 MIDI notes {67, 63}; Track 2 MIDI notes {65, 62}."* **Both tracks play the same `MOTIF`** — `addTrack(0)` and `addTrack(roundOff)` over one shared array — so Track 2's pitch set is {67, 63, 65, 62} too; what separates them is phase, and phase is a slider (`sources/5thOrgan.html:id="ro" value="14"@67`, range 1–56). Simulated over all 56 offsets × 16 repetitions: **safe only at 8–20 and 36–48**; 1–7 collide 32–192 times, 21–35 collide 30–180, 49–56 collide 28–168. Nothing hangs — every note-on has a matching note-off — but `sources/5thOrgan.html:v.startTime > best.startTime@266` releases the **newest** matching voice, so the two notes exchange durations and the canon audibly deforms. The default 14 sits safely mid-band, **and the report's own test script step 5 says *"Set Round Offset to 1"*, the worst value in the range.** (Its step 6, *"Set Round Offset to 0"*, cannot be performed at all — `min="1"` and `sources/5thOrgan.html:function gRO()@340` clamps.)
> **Fix (both):** rebuild `seqEvents` at the loop boundary from the current control values and derive the advance from the rebuilt array's own span instead of recomputing it independently — that closes (a) outright and makes (b) a *display* problem, solvable by tagging each event with its track index and matching `noteOff` on `(midi, track)` rather than on pitch alone. **Verify:** a headless run asserting (i) event times change after a mid-play BPM edit and (ii) no two simultaneously-active voices share a MIDI note at any offset in 1–56. **Sequence after §AUDIO-01's design call** — if the answer is option (a) iframe, fix it in `sources/5thOrgan.html`; if option (b), fix it during extraction.

### §DX-02ar — the quest dependency graph still reads the format §ARCH-01 retired, and the delete guard is fed by it (NEW 2026-08-12 during §DOC-02ag, 🟡 no design call on the diagnosis, a small one on the fix's scope)

- [ ] **§DX-02ar — `WBAPI.quests.chain()` derives every dependency edge from an `S_story.` regex over raw quest source, so the declarative 96 % of `QUEST_DB` is invisible to it.** `lab-report-quest-api-architecture.md` §1.3 filed this as a defect in 2026-05-28 (*"The WBAPI flag extraction currently relies on regex over raw source text as a workaround. This is fragile."*) and §10 promised the fix by name (*"Chain graph — `WBAPI.quests.chain(id)` — uses declarative `gate.flags` instead of regex"*). **The migration shipped and the analyser did not move.** `js/wbapi-core.js:this._questFlags[id] = { reads, writes };@797` still populates `_questFlags` from `src.matchAll(/S_story\.(\w+)/)` over each entry's source text, and `js/wbapi-core.js:chain(id) {@1089` reads `_questFlags` / `_flagToQuests` and nothing else — there is no `gate.flags` branch anywhere in the file.
> **Migrating to a declarative format therefore made the analyser blind, because a declarative gate contains no `S_story.` token to match.** Measured over all 2,853 quests: **104** contain any `S_story.` read and **66** a write; **1,680** carry declarative dependency terms (`gate.flags` / `flagsAny` / `notFlags` / `questsDone` / `questsAttempted`); **1,624 of those 1,680 have no `S_story.` token at all.** So `chain(id)` returns `{upstream:[],downstream:[]}` for **2,749 of 2,853 quests (96.4 %)**. The 2,449 `mission_bit` grants are invisible for the same reason on the write side — the flag is set by a host effect (`mission_bit(bit, ctx) {@22303`), never by an assignment in the quest's own text.
> **The consequence is not cosmetic: it disarms a safety guard.** `js/wbapi-core.js:const d=WBAPI._deps.quest(k); if(d.downstream.length)@1107` is the refusal that stops `./api.sh del quest` removing a quest other quests gate on, and `js/wbapi-core.js:quest(id) { return { downstream:@848` feeds it from that same empty chain. For 96 % of the database the guard passes vacuously, and `advise` reports the empty chain as fact.
> ***This is the §DX-02n family inverted once more — not a structure with no readers, but a live analyser still reading the format its own specification retired.*** It is also the third distinct blind spot in the same census machinery (after §DX-02ao's `_flagToQuests` scope note and §DX-02ac's `||`-branch class): **the scan universe, not the scan, is what keeps being wrong.**
> **Fix (no design call on the core):** add a declarative pass beside the regex — walk `q.gate` / `q.completion` for `flags` / `flagsAny` / `notFlags` / `flagEquals` / `questsDone` / `questsAttempted` / `items` / `battles` into `reads`, and walk `q.bits` / `q.onComplete` recursively (through `skill_check.onPass`/`onFail` and `choice.options[].bits`) for `mission_bit.flag` and `flag_write.set`/`clear` into `writes`. Keep the regex for the 144 quests that still carry a closure. **Small scope call:** whether `questsDone` edges should be reported as the same kind of edge as flag edges or as a separate `sequence` edge — recommend separate, since a quest-completion edge is a stronger claim than a shared flag. **Verify:** `WBAPI.quests.chain('quest_wis_02')` must name `quest_wis_01`'s hook writer upstream; a corpus assertion that the count of quests with an empty chain drops from 2,749 to under ~200; and a `del quest` on a gated quest must be refused.

### §DX-02as — four bit-contract surfaces validate green and do nothing, and the block's own comment miscounts its exceptions (NEW 2026-08-12 during §DOC-02ag, 🟢 no design call)

- [ ] **§DX-02as — `const BIT_CONTRACTS = {@21970` accepts four things no code path consumes.** The registry is the authority on what a UQF bit may contain (§ARCH-01 §9), and `function validateQuest(q) {@22004` is the checker every Playwright corpus sweep runs. Four entries pass validation and have no effect:
> **(a) `skill_check.adv`** — listed `optional` since Phase 1, and `_rollSkill(stat) {@22242` never reads `bit.adv`. **Advantage is unreachable through UQF**, though the mechanic exists elsewhere in the engine (`_drunkFight`'s `adv='dis'`). 0 authored uses.
> **(b) `narrative.template`** — `narrative(bit, ctx) { if (!bit.msg) return;@22301` returns immediately, so a `template`-only bit is a **silent no-op**. The renderer it names, `renderNamedTemplate`, **never shipped as a function** — it survives only inside that handler's own trailing comment (*"template path: Phase 2 renderNamedTemplate"*). 0 authored uses. This is also the standing answer to the report's Open Question #1, and the answer is *nothing was built*: multi-state node surfaces went to `NODE_PANELS`/`NODE_HOOKS`/`NODE_VERBS` instead.
> **(c) `unlock.npcs`** — the sharpest of the four, because the dead field *satisfies the validator on its own*: `validate: b => ((b.quests||[]).length + (b.npcs||[]).length) > 0`. `unlock(bit, ctx) { (bit.quests@22312` ignores `npcs` entirely, so `{kind:'unlock', npcs:['brynn']}` validates ✅ and does nothing at all. 0 authored uses — today.
> **(d) the whole `item_check` kind** — contract, handler and all: `item_check(bit, ctx) {@22311` writes `ctx._itemCheck`, which **nothing in the file reads**. 0 authored uses across 2,853 quests. It was built to answer the report's Open Question #3 (*"completeItems → does this become `gate.items`, or a new bit kind?"*) and **both answers were built**; only the completion-gate `items` term is used.
> **(e) The block's own comment miscounts the population it describes.** `function adaptLegacyQuest(id, q) {@22026` states the surviving non-UQF entries are *"quest_math_01–05 §MATH-01 gap + the 30 dead blq_05–10 book-stubs"* — **35**. Measured through the `wbapi-core` parse: **50**. The fifteen omitted are `quest_1367_a`–`f`, `quest_lxvii67`, `quest_guide_04`, `quest_scar_01`–`04` and `quest_void_tide_21/35/42`. Nine of them are named *as migrated* in their own wave commit messages (`ac9ef23` Wave 1r scar arc, `cdc788f` Wave 1v lxvii67/guide_04), so their bits and gates were converted and only the `schema:` stamp was missed. `advise` already flags each one individually; only the summary is wrong. ***A migration commit's comment is a claim about the present as well as the past, and it is the claim least likely to be re-measured.***
> **Fix:** (a) read `bit.adv` in `_rollSkill` (roll 2d20 keep-high / keep-low, matching `_rollCeremonia`'s existing advantage path) **or** drop it from the contract — recommend implementing it, since advantage on a check is a mechanic the game already has and 2,623 `skill_check` bits could use; (b)+(d) drop `template` and `item_check` from the registry, leaving the comment as a tombstone; (c) either handle `npcs` or remove it from both `optional` and the `validate` sum — the sum is the bug regardless; (e) stamp `schema:'UQF-1.0'` on the nine already-migrated entries and correct the comment to the measured figure. **Verify:** `validateQuest({id:'x',schema:'UQF-1.0',bits:[{kind:'unlock',npcs:['x']}]}).valid` must be `false`; a corpus assertion that every contract key is either exercised by ≥1 authored bit or explicitly listed as reserved.

### §DX-02at — the bit vocabulary lives in two hand-maintained copies and the editor's copy has drifted (NEW 2026-08-12 during §DOC-02ag, 🟢 no design call)

- [ ] **§DX-02at — `worldbuilder.html:const OPERAND_CONTRACTS = {@1373` holds 11 kinds; `const BIT_CONTRACTS = {@21970` holds 13.** The editor's own header comment says it *"mirrors the game's BIT_CONTRACTS (QuestRuntime registry)"*. It no longer does. **Missing: `cost`** — the §VM-01-G4a price leaf, a live opcode with three authored uses and the newest mechanic in the language — **and `_legacy_fn`**, with 115. So the authoring tool cannot describe, and its operand UI cannot offer, the one bit kind that makes a mission charge the player.
> **This is the §ARCH-01 §1 argument turned on its author.** That document exists because *"quest behavior currently lives in three places simultaneously"*; the format it defined now has its vocabulary in two, kept in sync by hand, and the drift arrived with the first opcode added after the editor was written. It is the same shape as §DX-02ad (a doc declaring itself the register of a `const` and naming a fraction of it), one layer down: **a second definition of a data contract is a doc about that contract, whatever file it lives in.**
> **Fix (two lines, then the durable version):** add the `cost` and `_legacy_fn` rows now; then make the mirror derived rather than typed — `worldbuilder.html` already loads the game file through `wbapi-core`, so the kind list can be read out of the `QUEST:CORE` region (`// ◆◆◆ QUEST:CORE:START ◆◆◆@21965` … `QUEST:CORE:END`) at parse time, leaving `OPERAND_CONTRACTS` to carry only the editor-side prose columns (`gate:` / `complete:` descriptions) keyed by kind. **Verify:** a test asserting `Object.keys(OPERAND_CONTRACTS)` ⊇ `Object.keys(BIT_CONTRACTS)` minus an explicit `NOT_AUTHORABLE` list (`_legacy_fn` is a fair member of that list; `cost` is not).

### §DX-02aq — the Necklace of Knowledge is a minority writer into its own array, and the other fourteen render as `undefined` (NEW 2026-08-12 during §DOC-02af, 🟡 no design call on the fix, a small one on the surface)

- [ ] **§DX-02aq — `S_story.knowledge` carries two incompatible value shapes and the renderer tests neither.** Layer 13's Necklace shipped exactly as its spec wrote it: `function _maybeAddKnowledgeBead@25808` pushes `{ name, icon, node, type:'knowledge' }`, byte-exact to `lab-report-prompt-migration-arena-to-prototype.md` and to `lab-report-drop-rates-balance-and-health.md` (§DOC-02j verified the same record independently). **It is now 1 of 15 push sites.** The other fourteen push a **bare string** — investigation lore notes from the Warmth arc (`The Warmth: a colonial microorganism…`), the Deep Warmth Eel, the Relay Road, the Lake, the Dunfall Drift Spore, the Bilge Mystery, Roen's Personal Legend, Ardley's Laws ×2, the Cycle-4 archive note, the Atlantean Foundation note and the Crone Bead ×2 — plus `st.knowledge.push(bit.knowledge)@22276`, the UQF `reward` bit's clue field, which forwards whatever a quest author wrote.
> **The defect is player-visible in the panel whose whole purpose is legibility.** The inventory renderer at `S_story.knowledge.forEach(bead@31231` builds each row as `bead.icon` + `bead.name` + a `memory` tag with **no type test**. On a string primitive both properties are `undefined`, so **every lore note renders under 🔮 Necklace of Knowledge as the literal row `undefinedundefined memory`** — one row per note. A player who has run any of those arcs sees a necklace of `undefined`s beside their real beads.
> **No gate can see it, and the reason is structural:** this is a *field-shape* contract, not a node, npc or quest reference. `check:noderegs` / `check:npcregs` / `check:dupkeys` / `check:questgraph` are all blind to it, and so is §DX-02n's proposed `check:deadconsts` — the field has plenty of readers and plenty of writers; what it lacks is agreement between them. It is the **inverse** of the §DX-02n family: not a structure with zero readers, but **one reader serving two incompatible writer shapes**.
> **Both designs are documented, independently, and neither knows about the other.** The bead half is specified in two 2026-05-21 lab reports; the clue-store half is this file's own mystery-arc row, which cites `S_story.knowledge[]` as an existing cumulative-clue store and the same `.inv-item-knowledge@1546` / `.inv-item-knowledge@3238` CSS as its render path. **Fix (no design call):** normalise on write — wrap a string push as `{ name: <the text>, icon:'📖', type:'lore' }`, or normalise on read with a `typeof bead === 'string'` branch in the renderer. **Small design call on the surface only:** whether lore notes belong in the Necklace section at all, or in their own 📖 Field Notes section beneath it — they are a different kind of memory (what you learned vs. where you slept), and the report's own thesis is that a bead means *"I was here"*. Recommend a separate section plus a normalising writer, so the Necklace stays the geography it was designed to be. **Verify:** a test asserting every element of `S_story.knowledge` has a string `name` and a string `icon` after each of the fifteen push sites, and that the rendered panel contains no `undefined`.

### §DX-02ao / §DX-02ap — the Mission Explorer shipped as `worldbuilder.html` and dropped the one requirement the user stated in their own words (NEW 2026-08-12 during §DOC-02ae)

- [ ] **§DX-02ao — no Explorer view emits a JavaScript reference path, a data type, or an array position.** 🟡 **small design call, on form only.** `lab-report-ponies-unicorns-aspirations-future-ideas.md` §III.C quotes the requirement verbatim: *"give all the debug information about the variable name, about the data type, about its index and position where we can reference it to change it."* The spec then made it concrete — three things per field: the JS read path (`MONSTER_POOL["goblin_scout"].ac`), the data type (`string` / `number` / `boolean` / `array[N]`), and the position (array index, object key, or HTML line). The Explorer **shipped** as `worldbuilder.html` (10,685 lines, 17 tabs, birth `2d42ea2` 2026-05-29) with the Bestiary / NPCs / Quests / Mission tabs the spec asked for — and **none of the three metadata rows**. Measured: 6 occurrences of a `NAME[` path shape in the whole file, all of them patch-generation or audit-advice strings, none in a detail view; `typeof` appears 21 times, every one a validator; the CRUD tab's *"Type"* control is an **entity**-type selector (node/quest/monster/npc/terrain), not a data-type annotation.
> **What shipped instead answers the other half of the sentence.** The Wizard and Builder tabs emit the **API call** that mutates the record, so *"reference it to change it"* is served and *"where it lives"* is not. That is better for authoring and strictly worse for comprehension — the stated target user is *"a modder or a curious developer who wants to understand the architecture without reading 14,377 lines of source"*, and they still have to read the source to find out where a value lives.
> **Fix — the data is already in hand.** `wbapi-core` parses the section, so the key, the containing const and the index are known at render time; the type is `typeof`; the line number is already computed by the source-level writers (`WBAPI.deleteEntrySource` locates entries by line today). **Design call is which form:** (a) an always-on third column in each detail view; (b) a "dev metadata" toggle in the header, off by default, so the tables stay readable; (c) a click-to-copy path chip beside each value. **Recommend (b) + (c).** **Verify:** open the Bestiary detail for any monster and copy a path that pastes into a browser console against the live game and returns the shown value.
> **Half of §III.B's State Flag Browser is already built and nobody has noticed.** `worldbuilder.html:this._flagToQuests[f].writes.push(id)@1695` maintains a per-flag reader/writer index — exactly the spec's *"which quest/arc sets it"* row — but its scan universe is the `QUEST_DB` source text only, so the *"which render functions read it"* row is structurally absent. **That is the same blind spot `check:deadconsts` (§DX-02n) keeps rediscovering from the other side, and this is prior art for it:** the census exists, it is simply pointed at one section of the file. Widen the scan universe rather than starting over.

- [ ] **§DX-02ap — the authoring tool hands the author a runnable raw-`curl` sequence.** 🟢 **no design call.** `worldbuilder.html:Full curl sequence (run in order)@7929` renders a copy-and-run block of `curl -s -X POST ${FS_API}/node|/monster|/quest -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '…'` lines built by the Wizard's review step (3 push sites). That is precisely the shape prompt.md §3's golden rule and CONTRIBUTING Hazard #7 forbid — *"all world-building goes through `./api.sh`… never use raw `curl` for authoring"* — emitted by the authoring tool itself, so it teaches the hazard rather than merely tolerating it. **It is invisible to every gate:** §DX-02l-FU deliberately narrowed the detector to *"a line an author can copy and run"*, which these are, but the detector's file universe is `.md` only and `worldbuilder.html` is not in it.
> **Fix:** emit `./api.sh post node code=… label=… act=… name=…` equivalents in the review block (keep the curl lines behind a "raw HTTP" disclosure if they are wanted for debugging). **Do NOT touch the Endpoints tab** — its curl examples are an HTTP reference for the API surface itself, which is the one legitimate use, and the same distinction §DX-02l-FU drew for the docs. **Verify:** `grep -c "curl -s -X POST" worldbuilder.html` outside the Endpoints block = 0.

### §DX-02ac — eight dead `||` fallback literals name a starting character the game has never made, and four documents believed them (NEW 2026-08-12 during §DOC-02w, 🟢 no design call)

- [ ] **§DX-02ac — `const s = S_story.abilityScores || { str:16, dex:12, con:14, int:10, wis:12, cha:8 };@23439` and seven siblings.** The `||` branch is unreachable: `abilityScores: { str:10, dex:8, con:8, int:8, wis:8, cha:8 },@23046` is declared in `_S_DEFAULTS()` and `const scores = startScores || { str:10, dex:8, con:8, int:8, wis:8, cha:8 };@23952` re-asserts it on every new game, so `abilityScores` is never absent. The `16/12/14/10/12/8` statline **has never been a starting character** — not at HEAD, not at `0a131f5`, not at any point measured. `grep -c` finds it **8 times** across the file as a `||` fallback.
> **The cost is not dead weight, it is four wrong documents.** `lab-report-luck-seventh-stat.md` §II-A read the fallback as the default and built its flagship worked example on it (*"Starting Human Fighter (STR 16, DEX 12, CON 14, INT 10, WIS 12, CHA 8) … Luck 12, Mod +1"*; the real default is **Luck 9, Mod −1**). That example propagated into `lab-report-fishing-bait-prompting.md`'s Appendix B and into **`mechanics.md:356`** and **`docs/mechanics/mechanics-combat.md:344`**, all four printing *"Default scores (STR:16, DEX:12, CON:14…)"*. ***A write-only field is inert; a dead `||` branch that names a plausible data shape reads exactly like a declaration.*** Sixth widening of the proposed `check:deadconsts` — after top-level consts, quest-entry fields, parameters, item objects and `||`-chain alternatives (§DX-02n (e)), this is the first where the alternative is a **plausible-looking literal** rather than an identifier, so a reader/writer census cannot even see the question.
> **Fix:** collapse all eight to `S_story.abilityScores` (or to a single named `const _DEFAULT_SCORES` that equals `_S_DEFAULTS()`'s value), then correct the four documents. Verify with `grep -c "str:16, dex:12, con:14"` = 0.

### §DX-02ad — `quest.md` calls itself the register of *all* quests and names 148 of 2,853 (NEW 2026-08-12 during §DOC-02x, 🟢 no design call)

- [ ] **§DX-02ad — a bijection that shipped, was declared canonical, and quietly stopped being true; §DOC-02i's FC01 class in a second subject.** `quest.md`'s own Purpose line reads *"Location-organized register of **all quests** — implemented, planned, and specced,"* and `lab-report-meta-process-loop-expansion.md` recommendation 8 is where the claim was written down (*"The register is the canonical source of truth for quest IDs, locations, and act structure"*). Measured through the canonical `wbapi-core` parse — the same extractor `:1367` and every `scripts/check-*.js` use: **`QUEST_DB` holds 2,853 entries across 57 id prefixes; `quest.md` names 148 of them (5.2 %).** Broken down: the hand-authored `quest_*` family is **145 of 298 (48.7 %)**, and the other **56 families hold 2,555 quests of which 3 are named** (`ada` 235 · `ath` 120 · `lis` 95 · `zth` 80 · `flr` 75 · `blq` 60 · `kya` 60 · `hft`/`rkv`/`ost`/`rix`/`jrs` 55 each · …). **⟶ SECOND SUBJECT, SAME SHAPE, 2026-08-12 (§DOC-02ab).** `docs/story/story-arc-npc-dialogues.md` headed its transcript *"Source: `NPC_DIALOGUES` const … 6 NPCs × 4 states × 5 quotes = 120 lines"* while `const NPC_DIALOGUES = {@10396` holds **213 entries and 1,614 quotes** — a complete and accurate transcript of **2.8 %** of the table, wrong only by omission, so every spot-check passes. Its per-NPC arithmetic was off too: all six Birka pools are 5/5/5/**4**, so the true figure is **114**, not 120. Both corrected in place. **So the gate this row wants should be scoped to *any doc that declares itself the register of a named data section*, not to `quest.md` alone.** Cheap general form: if a doc's own prose names a `const` **and** a count, re-derive the count from that `const` through `wbapi-core` and fail on a mismatch.
> **The reverse direction is SPOTLESS, and that is why nobody has caught it.** Thirteen quest-shaped tokens in `quest.md` fail to resolve in `QUEST_DB` and **not one is a dead row**: ten are deliberate annotations of the form `` `quest_d0207_a1–a5` *(design: quest_cy_madness_gate)* `` — live id first, design-era name preserved beside it, which is the same discipline that let §DOC-02k score §DUNGEON-01 rather than guess at it — and the other three are prose fragments. ***So the register is wrong only by OMISSION and never by ASSERTION: everything it says is true, and it says it about one quest in nineteen.*** That is the hardest staleness to notice, because every spot-check passes — the §DOC-02i mechanism exactly (*a check that depends on a human running it reports green when nobody ran it*).
> **Fix — the cheapest gate in the family, a two-way `comm` over the parser's own key list.** `check:questindex`: `WBAPI.load()` → `Object.keys(questDb)` vs the ids `quest.md` cites. Two explicit classification lists, both in the §AUDIT-03j house style rather than a heuristic: **`NOT_A_QUEST_ID`** for the `*(design: …)*` aliases and prose fragments, and a **generated-family exemption list** naming each bulk prefix with a reason, so the register is scored against the population it is actually meant to cover. **The exemption must be written down, not inferred** — a percentage heuristic is blind to a family that is *entirely* generated, which is the same argument gates #13/#14/#16 each had to make.
> **Then decide the register's scope in one sentence and put it in `quest.md`'s Purpose line**, because "all quests" has not been true since the bulk families landed and the doc has never said so.

### §DX-02ae — a render getter writes a progression flag, and a scene comment disagrees with its own guard (NEW 2026-08-12 during §DOC-02y, 🟢 no design call)

- [ ] **§DX-02ae (a) — `ACT8_FAREWELL_BEATS.brynn.text` is a `text: () => {…}` accessor that MUTATES `S_story`.** Rendering the Act VIII Brynn farewell runs `lampLine = BRYNN_KEEPER_STORY.farewellNoStory;@26893` and, on the next line, `S_story.brynnKeeperStoryTold = true`. The write is **correct as design** — `farewellNoStory` is a catch-up delivery (*"There's a lamp in the corner that's been burning since your first night. I wanted you to know that."*), so the player who never found Beat 1 does now know, and the epilogue row keyed on that flag reads truthfully. **The hazard is the placement, not the write.** Two downstream consumers read it: the Town Crier's `qOrder = @26865` (which is where the lamp news actually ships, under `brynnKeeperStoryTold:      'The lamp at the First Inn@26775`) and `_buildEpilogueScroll`. It is safe today **only because `_renderNpcCard` sets its `act8Farewell<Key>` latch BEFORE invoking `beat.text()`** — remove that ordering, add a preview render, or call the getter twice for any reason, and the branch silently advances from `farewellNoStory` to `farewellNoChoice` with no error. **Fix:** move the flag write to the call site, beside the latch, and leave `text()` pure. ***A render accessor that mutates progression state is one refactor away from a double-fire, and nothing in the type system or the gates can see the coupling.***
- [ ] **§DX-02ae (b) — `const YAEL_NAMED_REPORT_SCENE = {@28048`'s own `// → doc:` comment says *"fav >= 2 Act IV+"* and the guard says Act VI.** `if (node.code === 'LHR' && _npcFavor('yael') >= 2@32489` is followed by `(S_story.actNumber || 1) >= 6`. One line apart, in the same file, and the annotation is the half a doc reader trusts. One-word fix; recorded because the `// → doc:` corpus is 93 annotations and nothing audits their *contents* (§DOC-02x).

> **Three deltas worth keeping.** (1) **The self-funding thesis holds on two of three axes:** the heal is clamped to `hpMax` (`10 + CON mod` at level 1, `+d10 + CON mod` per level), so the heal axis **saturates** wherever `0.1 × AC × maxHP ≥ hpMax` — at level 1 that is nearly the whole pool, four of the report's own five rows are simply "full heal", and *"the dragon… heals you for 807 HP"* can never happen at any level. The engine is right; the rhetoric reads a saturating axis as a linear one. (2) **The rest architecture shipped inverted** — §III-B explicitly declines the 5e model for the short rest (*"Rather than Hit Die rolls…"*) and HEAD does exactly that, then ships **Hit Die rolls on the long rest**, so the specified DGQR full-HP restoration never landed. (3) The quest-boost pillar is **RETIRED**, not stale (tombstone at `` `§TIMELESS-01: Stalk Helpers@38269` ``). Stale counts: 42 nodes → **416**, 8 inns → **38**, ½-HP respawn → **1 HP** (1 at the archive too, so wrong when written).

Existing-Work-First: tree clean at `5d64e89`, one other claude process, `:1367` verified **free** the whole session (Hazard #1 — this slice hand-edits inline JS), and `grep -c NODE_VERBS` returned **0** in both `roll2hit-v3.html` and `js/quest.js`, so the row's premise held. **Shipped:** `NODE_VERBS` + `_renderNodeVerbs` — the third small vocabulary beside `NODE_PANELS` (flavour a node *shows*) and `NODE_HOOKS` (an interface a node *owns*) — and Kern & Sable's **76 inline lines** at DUS as its three entries (Q-NEXUS-00/01/02, the Torment Nexus overture). **The design finding is that §9.1's locked schema was for the wrong half of Class D.** The lab report locked `{id, nodes, when, label, bits}` — a **button** verb, which is the D1 shape it was measured against. A **D2 exclusive choice has no button**: the options *are* the surface. Giving Kern & Sable a `label` would have inserted a click the player never had to make, so the entry's mode is decided by what it carries — **`label`+`bits`** = a button that runs the chain on click · **`bits` with no `label`** = the chain IS the surface, so it runs at render and its first bit **must** park on a `choice` · **`ambient`** alone = a flavour line for a state with nothing to do. That third mode is where the slice earned its keep: running a chain at render is exactly how side effects land on every draw of a node, so a label-less non-suspending chain is refused with a warning — **and refused BEFORE its mount is created.** The first implementation refused *after* inserting the mount and the test caught it: **a refusal that leaves an empty div behind is not a refusal, it is a page that changed anyway.** **Two behaviour deltas, both named in the diff rather than discovered in play:** (1) the driver re-renders when a chain ends, so the Q-NEXUS-01 follow-up now appears **in the same beat** as [Ask] instead of on the next arrival, and the aftermath line lands the moment Q-NEXUS-02 completes — the fiction supports it (they are still at the counter, waiting), it is asserted in the test file, and `story.md`'s *"next `DUS` visit"* wording is **kept and annotated as authored intent** rather than rewritten; (2) the **empty 8px spacer div** the inline block always inserted — visible as dead space in the "listened and walked away" state — is gone. **Evidence, in the order it was built.** (a) An **authored-string multiset diff** between HEAD's block and the new table: **14 vs 14, identical, nothing added or lost**, with the three ambient lines unwrapped from the `innerHTML` wrapper the old code hand-built. This is G2b's line-multiset method adapted to a block that **could not** move verbatim — its shape changed, so only its content can be pinned, and pinning the content is what proves no prose was retyped from a screenshot. (b) A **golden-DOM diff of all four DUS states** against HEAD (temp harness, deleted): text and button labels **byte-identical, including the 6px/4px button spacing** — `_uqfRenderAsk` was given the first-button 6px that every hand-written option panel in the file uses, so the migration is pixel-identical rather than merely equivalent. What remains is the mount's `id`, a `data-uqf-option` attribute, one redundant wrapper `<div>` + `<em>` dropped from an already-italic `.npc-ambient` (CSS 2122 — zero pixels), and delta 2. (c) **`uqf-node-verbs.test.js` 10/10, with all 10 failing at HEAD.** That is deliberately **not** G2b's "some tests pass both ways" shape, and saying so is the honest part: the surface's DOM identity changed with the migration, so the before/after equivalence has to live in the golden diff, not in the after-state contract — and the test file says that in its own header. Plus `check:walk` **16/16 exit 0** with `check:questparity` at **25,030 bytes — the kernel was not touched**, this slice is entirely host code (G4a spent the track's one parity-fence edit); full Playwright **826 passed / 4 failed** = the documented `worldbuilder-crud-arrays` four; and **§7½ eyeballed** in the running game — all three states screenshotted, the sidebar ITEMS counter ticking **0→1** as the token lands through `reward`, and the newline-collapsing in `#story-move-msg` checked against HEAD and confirmed **pre-existing** (`storyMsg` sets `textContent` on an element with no `pre-wrap`, before and after). One thing factored rather than duplicated: `_mkAmbientLine` is now the single definition a `choice` prompt and a `NODE_VERBS` `ambient` both use, so they cannot drift. Docs: lab report **§12¾** + 5 new anchors, `quest.md` §"`NODE_VERBS` — where a verb is authored", `story.md` §Q-NEXUS + `world.md` annotated, `prompt.md` §4 + §7 (baseline 816→**826**), `anchors:fix` for the 113 hints my +39 net HTML lines drifted. **Next: G4c** — the 13 D1 verbs → `NODE_VERBS` (the button mode now has a registry to land in) plus converting the Junction Vignette `[Help — 10gp]` to `cost`, which is the parent's stated bar for the leaf not being single-use. Then G4d (CDG's concurrent menu + the two Class-E strays → `NODE_HOOKS`).

> **⟶ PRIOR (2026-08-04) — §VM-01-G4a ✅ SHIPPED `b905733`: the `choice` opcode has a host end at last, and the `cost` leaf says the price out loud.** On "continue" the user answered the one ASK the G4 design lock was waiting on — **(a) refuse-at-click**, the recommendation — which unblocked the only row on the whole board that needed no further design call. Existing-Work-First: tree clean at `32845cd`, `:1367` verified free the whole session (Hazard #1 — this slice hand-edits inline JS), and greps for `_uqfRunVerb` / `NODE_VERBS` / `cost` returned **nothing**, so the row's premise held. **Zero content moved, exactly as §10 sliced it** — G4a is the seam, G4b is its first consumer. **Shipped, kernel side (`js/quest.js`, inside QUEST:CORE → re-inlined, parity green at 25,030 bytes):** the **`cost`** opcode, registered next to `reward` because it is `reward`'s inverse and because `reward` is precisely how you get this wrong — `gold:-50` computes correctly with no affordability test, no refusal and the word *reward* on a price, Hazard #2's *a write into a real-but-wrong object never throws*. Contract `{gold?, resource?, count?, refuse?}`; **every currency is tested before any is spent**, so a mixed price can never part-pay — a property the design report measured toward but never named, and the one a naive leaf breaks silently. The leaf needed a mechanism the VM did not have — **chain failure**: a handler may set `ctx._halt` and `execBits` breaks on it. It is **deliberately never cleared in the loop**, because `ctx` is shared with the nested `execBits` a `choice` option runs: clearing it would let the bits *after* an unpaid branch run on. One `ctx` per run is what makes a sticky flag safe, and both drivers build a fresh one. **Shipped, host side (outside the fence, beside `_uqfPump`):** `_uqfRunVerb`/`_uqfRenderAsk` — the half Inc A never wrote. An `{ask:'choice'}` envelope now renders one button per option into the verb's own mount, resumes the **same** generator with the picked index, and on completion removes the mount and re-renders the node with the chain's narrative as `storyRender`'s **prefix** (`_resolveQuestUQF`'s route — the tail `storyMsg` would otherwise overwrite it, §BOARD-01-FU6). Two properties designed in rather than discovered: `storyRender` **abandons** a pending generator beside the sweep that takes its panel's DOM (Inc A's single slot assumed *"a choice resolves within one interaction turn"*; a NODE choice can sit across a render — and abandoning writes nothing, because `choice` applies the picked option's bits only *after* the pick), and a stale option button **re-checks that the slot still holds its own generator**, so a click on a survived panel is inert rather than resuming a dropped chain. **The scope fence is untouched:** a `choice` inside `skill_check`'s `onPass`/`onFail` still throws, so a `require('./quest')` server still needs no host driver. **Evidence:** new `uqf-verb-driver.test.js` **12/12**, and **the positive control is the shape that matters — against HEAD 10 of 12 fail, and the 2 that pass are exactly the two asserting *unchanged* behaviour** (a chain with no `cost` runs every bit; a `choice` in a skill-check branch still throws). `check:walk` **16/16 exit 0** (`check:questparity` byte-identical both ways). Full Playwright **816 passed / 4 failed** = the documented `worldbuilder-crud-arrays` four. **The first run reported 815/5, and the fifth red was mine and was correct**: `quest-runtime-uqf.test.js:28` pins the entire `HANDLERS` key list precisely so a new opcode cannot enter the table unrecorded — adding `cost` to the pin is part of the fix, not a concession to it, and it is the fourth time this repo has been told something by a test rather than by a grep. **No §7½** — nothing player-visible changed, because nothing calls `_uqfRunVerb` yet and `cost` has no consumer until G4c; the whole point of the slice is that it is provable before a single block moves. Docs: lab report **§12½ addendum** (the ASK answered + what shipped), `prompt.md` §4 (the `cost` + driver contracts, incl. *`cost` never belongs in a `when`*) and §7 (baseline 804→**816**), **`quest.md` — a new "Prices and choices" section** so an author reaching for a price finds the leaf instead of writing the three inline lines a sixth time, and `anchors:fix` for the 113 hints my +115 HTML lines drifted. **Next: G4b — Kern & Sable, the first `choice` in the game's history, shipping alone so it can be eyeballed (§7½) without 13 migrations in the same diff.** Then G4c (13 D1 verbs → `NODE_VERBS` + the Junction Vignette `cost` conversion, which proves the leaf isn't single-use) → G4d.

> **⟶ PRIOR (2026-08-04) — §VM-01-G4 CHILD LAB REPORT ⚠️ DESIGN LOCKED PENDING ONE ASK `f340143` (the ASK is now ANSWERED — see NEWEST): the `choice` opcode Inc A shipped has no host end, and only a third of "Class D" is a choice at all.** On "continue" took the board's next-up (1) — the last migration slice, whose stated prerequisite was its own child design pass (the §VM-01-G lock: *"G4 OK in principle, but G4 gets its own child design pass first"*). Existing-Work-First: tree clean at `ca0113c`, **one** claude process, `:1367` verified free throughout, no `lab-report-vm01g4-*` existed, and every number re-measured live rather than carried from the parent. **The re-measurement is itself the track's evidence:** the region is **1,006 lines — 41% of the parent's 2,445** (front 33332→**33702**, in-region `node.code ===` 77→**29**), because G1+G2+G2b+G3 moved the front **forward 1,439 lines in seven days**. The parent's *"the front moves backward ~4/day"* is no longer true inside it. **Census: 22 blocks / 838 classified lines**, read end to end, not sampled. **Finding 1 — the keystone has no host end, and this reorders the whole slice.** Inc A built the coroutine correctly (`*execBits@22223`, the suspending `*choice@22319`, `_uqfPump@6827`, `_uqfPending@6824`) and the half that **renders the ask and resumes with an answer was never written**: `_uqfPump` has **exactly one** caller in the HTML — `_uqfRunToCompletion@6840`, which **throws** on an unresolved ask — **all four** live `execBits` entry points wrap in it (`6880`/`6883`/`30017`/`36843`), the fifth carries a comment saying *"a choice in onPass/onFail throws, by scope-fence"*, `_uqfPending` is **read by nothing** outside two integration tests, and **`renderChoiceBlock` occurs 0 times in `roll2hit-v3.html` and 0 times in `js/quest.js`** — it has never existed as code. §DX-01e-FU2 reached that from the anchor side; this reaches it from the call graph. **So a `choice` bit in any live quest today does not render a choice — it throws**, and G4 is `choice`'s first **HOST** consumer, not just its first content consumer. **G4a is therefore the driver, shipping with zero content migrated** — provable against the existing coroutine tests before one player-facing block moves. **Finding 2 — "Class D" is three shapes and `choice` fits one of them.** The parent's description fits the *click handler* of all 22 blocks and the *surface* of very few. Of **21 button surfaces: 13 are SINGLE VERBS** (one button, no alternative — a one-option choice is not a choice, it is a labelled effect chain with ceremony), **7 are exclusive CHOICES**, and **CDG's `cq-boss-buttons` is a CONCURRENT menu** whose Taz/Don/Cat-King confrontations are visible at once by design — mapping those onto an opcode that is *exclusive by construction* would be an outright **behaviour change**. So the vocabulary is **`NODE_VERBS {id, node, when, label, bits}`** in the `NODE_PANELS`/`NODE_HOOKS` house style (ordered registry, in-place dispatch → LIFO preserved by construction), with `choice` as a **bit inside it**, used only where the block is genuinely exclusive. Forcing one tool onto all of Class D would be the parent's own warning — *"this is how `itemsMinAny` happened, a shape grown for the wrong layer"* — coming true inside the slice written to honour it. **Grammar gap, measured rather than assumed:** the parent's *"`cost` leaf (gold≥N, consume) — ONE new opcode"* is half already shipped — **`item_remove@22302` covers every consume site** — and the missing half is **three currencies**: gold at **six** sites (Yva 50gp · the Junction Vignette `[Help — 10gp]`, which is the second consumer that proves the leaf isn't single-use · Kenickie's four prices), `surgeCharges` (spent permanently), and hp — and **hp is NOT a price**: the Memory Gate's −15 is narrated damage on a branch that always succeeds, so it belongs in that option's bits. Two shipped properties a naive leaf would silently change: **affordability is tested at CLICK, not at render** at every gold site, and **`reward` with negative gold "works"** arithmetically with no affordability test and the word *reward* on a price — Hazard #2's *a write into a real-but-wrong object never throws*. **Deliberately not migrated, each with its reason recorded so it doesn't read as an oversight:** Entry 42 (`S_story.entry42Text@34651`) and the ZRH void-toll rune (`S_story._voidTollSecret@34763`) capture **free text**, which `choice` cannot express *by design* (its resume value is an index *"so the data author never couples to presentation"*) and which a `prompt_text` ask for two sites would make the single-use term the Host/Script Separation Policy forbids — **grow it at three consumers, not two**; **Kenickie's Black Market (71 lines) and the Lower Archive launcher are Class E sitting in G4's region** and belong to `NODE_HOOKS` by G2's verbatim method — they fell between three slices (G2 deferred them, G2b found Kenickie *"is a CDG surface in G3's territory"*, G3 migrated activation not UI) and are recorded rather than dropped a fourth time; the Reading Circle is a **day-cooldown counter** whose repeat notion already lives in quests (`retryable`/`retryGateDays`). **The §VM-01-G2b act-leg thread is now closed for this region:** one comparison survives — `(S_story.actNumber || 1) >= 3@34691` at NUE — and **NUE is `act:6`, so it is vacuously TRUE, not dead**. Nothing to fix and nothing to file; deleting it would be an unverified rewrite of authored intent (§AUDIT-03m-FU). Recorded so the class is measured closed rather than assumed. **Slices locked: G4a** driver + `cost` (the only parity-fence edit in the track — `js/quest.js`, re-inline, `check:questparity`) · **G4b** Kern & Sable as the `choice` pilot (76 lines; no cost, no combat, no free text, one node — so the first choice in the game's history ships alone and can be eyeballed) · **G4c** the 13 D1 verbs → `NODE_VERBS` + convert the Junction Vignette Help to `cost` · **G4d** CDG's menu (as `combat` bits — **`combat`'s optional `nodeCode`@22135 already accepts the synthetic `CQ_TAZ` code those buttons use**) + the two Class-E strays. **Evidence:** `check:walk` **16/16 exit 0**; `check:anchors` **129 symbol anchors across 7 docs all resolve, 0 stale** — the lab report is the 7th doc and added 30 anchors, each verified individually, and **4 hints were off by one and were corrected by hand rather than left for `anchors:fix` to guess** (§DX-01e-FU: `--fix` picks the NEAREST hit). Docs only — **no HTML, no tests, no §7½**, Playwright untouched so the **804/4** baseline stands. **🟡 THE ONE ASK, and it blocks G4a:** when a verb is unaffordable, keep **refuse-at-click** (today's behaviour at all six gold sites, byte-identical, consistent with the track's telling-vs-asking thesis — **my recommendation**) or **gate at render** (tidier UI, but a real behaviour change at six sites and a quieter world)? The `cost` leaf's contract differs between the two, so G4a should not start until it is answered. **Next: answer the ASK → G4a; or §VM-01-G2b-FU / §DX-02m / §AUDIT-03d, all still waiting on their own design calls.**

> **⟶ PRIOR (2026-08-04) — §VM-01-G2b ✅ SHIPPED `bedf2c1`: the ctx design that blocked this slice was ONE FIELD — and moving the 29 blocks read five narrative beats out of the game that can never fire.** On "continue" with every §AUDIT-03 row still waiting on a user design call, took the active engineering track's open slice — the one whose blocker was an *engineering* decision, not a user one.
