The scan's apparent `n`/`row`/`txt`/`fav` hits were `\n` escapes inside strings, a word inside a comment, and block-local declarations, and the two candidates anyone would expect — `keys` and `_npcNodeKey` — are read by **none** of them. So the contract is `{ npcRowDiv }`, built once beside the anchor it carries; `_runNodeHook(id, node, ctx)` forwards it; **21** hooks destructure it in the signature and **8** take `(node)` alone and are asserted never to name the anchor. **Two safety properties checked BEFORE the move, because they are what makes a verbatim move legitimate:** no **top-level `return`** (all 13 sit inside click handlers — one at block level would have gone from exiting nothing to exiting a hook early) and no **`var`** (nothing hoists out of one block for a later one to read). **The single piece of evidence I would keep if I could keep only one: a line-multiset diff of the two revisions — nothing was removed except the 2 old `_runNodeHook` lines**, and every added line is scaffolding (29 fn headers, 29 closers, 29 registry entries, 29 dispatch calls, 13 comments, the ctx). All 895 moved lines are byte-identical; they were not even re-indented. **Behavioural proof: a 17-combo golden-DOM/state diff, 16 byte-identical.** The 17th (`HKG`) differed — and **differed again between two runs of the SAME code**, because the CY Madness Gate draws unseeded `Math.random()` into two *persisted* `S_story` fields. That is a pre-existing invariant-#6 violation, not a regression, and the after-vs-after run is what proves it rather than my say-so; filed as **§DX-02m** (51 sites; `check:rng` guards stream parity, so nothing gates *which* stream a state write draws from). **The finding: five act-gated beats in this region cannot fire.** `storyRender` sets `S_story.actNumber = node.act || 1` on every render, before the region, and every Birka node is `act:1` — so the lamp inquiry (`>=2`), the Heartwood letter (`>=4`), Yael's Named Report (`>=6`), the S54 joint witness (`>=7`) and the Act VIII Quill farewell (`===8`) are unreachable. **It cascades**: `birka-lamp-choice` waits on `brynnKeeperStoryTold`, and the dead Beat 1 is its only writer, so the §XXXV vigil arc past its ambient line is dead too. Same structurally-dead act leg **§VM-01-G3** retired from the quest stanzas — the third slice of this track to find that special-case code keyed on node state rots silently, which is the row's whole thesis. **Filed, not fixed**: G3 could drop its act legs because the other gate leaves already carried the staging; here the act leg *is* the staging, so something must replace it — and `world.md` §XXXIX designs Yael's scene for `LLA`/`HKG` at Act IV+ while the code fires at `LHR` at Act VI+, so neither number is trustworthy without corroboration (§AUDIT-03m-FU's laundering lesson). **§VM-01-G2b-FU** carries it, `world.md` + `story.md` are **annotated at all five sites** (annotate, never rewrite), and a test pins all five gates plus the cascade so the fix has to update it. **Evidence:** `check:walk` **16/16 exit 0** · new `uqf-npc-row-hooks.test.js` **8/8** with a **positive control** — against HEAD **5 of 8 fail**, and the 3 that pass are exactly the live-behaviour ones, which is the right shape: those test the game, not the migration · `uqf-node-hooks` 4/4 (its registry assertion now owns the G2 head explicitly) · full Playwright **804 passed / 4 failed** = the documented `worldbuilder-crud-arrays` four, with the known `multiplayer-presence:171` flake green 7/7 in isolation · inline `<script>` parses clean. **The `npcRowDiv` anchor class is now empty** (the only remaining references are the element's own construction, the ctx and the final insert), and G2's deferral list was approximate: **Kern & Sable is not an npc-row block** and **Kenickie** is a CDG surface in G3's territory — both recorded rather than quietly dropped. ### §VM-01 — The Quest VM → *No Word for Wait* (NEW 2026-07-16)

> **Diagnostic (parent) lab report:** `lab-reports/lab-report-javascript-mud.md` — a structural read of the entire `<script>` block (five layers, four execution traces: program/UI/movement/quest-acceptance), plus the follow-up verification recorded below. **Not** a quest-by-quest audit. **Inc A child lab report LOCKED 2026-07-21:** `lab-reports/lab-report-vm01a-execbits-coroutine.md` (design-review-before-implementation; locks the `execBits`→generator transformation, the `ask` envelope, the driver, the five call-site wraps, the three design calls, and the test plan — see §RESUME NEWEST banner above). Policy: **Host/Script Separation Policy** in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).
>
> **The unifying theme (matched to `story.md`): the engine tells, and cannot ask.** `story.md` is about a man who saw the Void and never managed to *ask anyone for help* — Froberger fixed it alone and it destroyed him. The quest engine commits the same act on the player: **you are told (`📋 <title>`), never asked.** Arrival + gate = `'active'`, announced in a `·`-joined message strip. There is no accept button — and the reason is not that nobody added one. **There is no state in which the VM is waiting for an answer.** (§PLAY-01 found the engine *knows what it won't transmit*; §VM-01 finds it **cannot receive**. Same sin, opposite direction.)
>
> **The architecture is already right — this track finishes §ARCH-01, it does not redesign it.** The file runs a proper embedded-scripting split twice over: three pure, world-injected, parity-fenced kernels (`MOVER`/`ROOMS`/`DUEL`, byte-identical to `js/*.js` with CI assertions), and a 258-line `QuestRuntime` executing 11,106 lines of `QUEST_DB` through the `BIT_CONTRACTS` opcode table. That 43:1 ratio is the achievement. **The defect is one small thing on top of it.**
>
> **Root cause — the VM has twelve opcodes and no jump instruction.** `execBits` (`execBits(bits, ctx)@22223`) in full: a `for` loop that looks up `HANDLERS[bit.kind]`, calls `h(bit, ctx)`, and ignores the return. No branch. No suspend. Three verified proofs, all grepped this session, none recalled:
>
> 1. **`choice` has a complete contract and an empty handler.** The contract (`choice:      { required@21997`) is rigorous — requires `prompt` + `options`, validates ≥2 options each carrying a `label` and a `bits` array. The implementation (`choice(bit@22319`) is, in full: `choice(bit, ctx) { /* Phase 2: renderChoiceBlock(bit.prompt, bit.options, ctx) */ }`. **Zero quests use it** (`grep -c "kind:'choice'"` → 0). It was never written because **a synchronous `for` loop cannot wait for a human being.**
> 2. **`item_check` writes a predicate nobody reads.** `ctx._itemCheck@22311` sets it; a full-file grep returns that line and nothing else. It is a conditional in a language with no `if` — it evaluates and evaporates.
> 3. **`skill_check` works only by smuggling.** It is the one bit that branches, and it does so by hardcoding the branch *inside the leaf*: `resolveSkillCheck` → `execBits(pass ? bit.onPass : bit.onFail)` (`execBits(pass ?@22259`). The sole conditional in the whole language is baked into one instruction rather than available to it.
>
> **Two missing words, and everything follows.** `wait` (no `yield` → no consent, no `choice`, no dialogue tree, no multi-step interaction, no `'abandoned'` status, no transactional bit chain — a throw mid-chain leaves half the effects applied with no rollback). `or` (no boolean nesting → each new OR shape has historically meant a new *term*; `itemsMinAny` was added for exactly one quest, `quest_wm_01`). **Prior art worth reading before Inc A:** Ink (Inkle) compiles narrative to JSON bytecode on a small VM and suspends at a `ChoicePoint` — structurally what this is; Yarn Spinner for dialogue; CEL / JSONLogic for Inc F (expression-AST-as-data, no parser needed).
>
> **Per Lab Report Policy: every increment locks its own child lab report (data shapes + flow) before any HTML edit.** The rows below are the *plan of a plan* — scope, evidence, dependency, and the decision each one carries. They are not implementation plans and must not be treated as one.
>
> **Dependency order:** A · B · C are independent (A is the keystone). D needs C. E needs C + the `_legacy_fn` purge. F is independent but cheaper after C. G needs A + F to be worth doing.

The doc was the thing that looked like evidence (§AUDIT-03l's class). **The row's own fix was blocked by a third defect: `PUT /api/terrain` accepted only `{label, icon}` — and persisted NOTHING.** It set `WBAPI.worldDb[k][f]` in memory, returned `ok:true` with the entity echoed, and never called `save()`; **`GET` then read the phantom edit back for the rest of the process's life**, so unlike the DELETE family (§DX-01d/i) the read path *corroborated* the lie. a dedicated **`WBAPI.editTerrainRoster(key, monsterKeys)`**, because `WORLD_DB` is the one collection whose array holds **code identifiers** (`P.giant_rat`) — `editStructuredField` would emit `["giant_rat"]`, which re-parses to strings and silently drives `_monsterLevel` to 1 for the whole terrain (§DX-01c's real-but-wrong-object, third dimension); it re-parses the patched section and **proves the roster reads back before committing** (`deleteEntrySource`'s refuse-rather-than-corrupt), the server re-verifies after the disk reload, and `editField` now **refuses** `monsters` outright (patchStringField would find no quoted value and insertStringField would add a *second* `monsters:` key — §AUDIT-03a's rot). **Duplicates are allowed, not rejected**, because `cat_quarter` ships one (`fluffy_cat` ×2) and a writer that cannot express what the corpus holds cannot round-trip it — it warns. **Then one `./api.sh put terrain sewers monsters=…` placed both void kin** (user-chosen: `sewers`' single node is **SFT "Visby Sewers"**, act 5, and Visby is where `VOID_TIDE_EVENTS[21]` sights the first Void Walker; levels 3 and 4 sit inside its `giant_rat`→`vampire` band). **Evidence:** the defect proved by round trip first (`ok:true` + `GET` agreeing + **0 occurrences in the file**); `git diff` on the game file for the placement = **exactly 1 line**; new `dx02h-terrain-roster-write.test.js` **6/6**, of which **5 fail on the stashed pre-fix tree** (restored, `shasum -c` OK — the one that passes is the inverse shape guard, already true); `check:walk` **15/15 exit 0**; - [x] **§DX-02i — `XP_BY_TIER` deleted; it was not a stale copy of the shipped XP model, it was a different one ✅ SHIPPED 2026-08-03 `a047348`.** Premise held: one occurrence, its own declaration. **User chose delete over annotate**, and the divergence was measured before removing it rather than asserted: the shipped formula is `(S.enemy.ac || 10) * (S.opp.maxHp || 10)` (in `_grantMissEffortXp`, with the §XP-01 dials as percentages of that product), and against it the table paid **1.9×–6.5× less at every tier** — `deadly` a flat 1000 against a shipped mean of **4,095** across 33 monsters (min 1,649, max 12,012), `medium` 100 against a mean of 638. So adopting it would have silently cut the whole curve, not merely rescaled it. **Deleting it cost four dependents**, which is why the cheaper "comment it" option was on the table: `dx02g-monster-tier-contract.test.js`'s `TIER_KEYED_SITES` entry (would have failed *anchor not found*), `dx01e-anchor-convention.test.js`'s resolver fixture (**swapped to `const EFFORT_XP_PCT`**, a live §XP-01 dial with exactly one occurrence), `check-npcregs.js`'s `NOT_NPC_KEYED` classification, and `index.md`'s Design Constants row — **whose text was itself wrong**, claiming the table was *"kept for reference — L12+ uses `AC × maxHP`"* when nothing consulted it at **any** level. A ten-line retirement note stands where the declaration was, naming the shipped formula and the measured ratios, so the next session that greps it finds the reason instead of a tempting table. **Side correction on the path:** the comment two lines below read *"Level 20 = 680,000 XP"* while `XP_LEVELS` ends at **195,000** — no entry has ever been 680,000; corrected in place (`index.md` had the right number all along). **Evidence:** `check:walk` **15/15 exit 0** (`anchors:fix` refreshed the 23 hints my ±9-line shift drifted); the §DX-02i assertion in `dx02h-terrain-roster-write.test.js` **fails on the pre-fix tree**; full Playwright **750 passed / 4 failed**, the documented four. *(The illustrative `XP_BY_TIER → XP_BY_TIER_RETIRED` rename examples in `scripts/resolve-anchors.js`'s comments are left alone — they are hypotheticals, and §DX-01e's ship record depends on that name for continuity.)* *(Original row: )* `const XP_BY_TIER = { trivial:25, easy:50, medium:100, hard:250, deadly:1000 };` had **one** occurrence in the file — its own declaration. Battle XP is computed as ≈`AC·maxHP` (and the §XP-01 effort grants are percentages of that), so this table is not merely unused, it encodes a *different* XP model than the one that ships — the exact "authoritative-looking but fictional" shape §AUDIT-03l warns about, one grep away from being wired up by a future session that assumes it is live. Decide: delete it, or comment it as a retired model. Do **not** wire it in without a balance pass — 2,850 quests and the whole level curve are calibrated against the shipped formula. **Risk:** none (delete) / high if naively adopted.

Original row follows. **§DX-02l-FU — the "no author-facing doc curls /api/save" assertion fails on PROSE about that very defect (found 2026-08-04 during §AUDIT-03k; a pre-existing red, not a regression).** `dx02l-save-snapshots-cli.test.js:190` flags any line in `api-user-guide.md` / `API-README.md` / `prompt.md` / `CONTRIBUTING.md` containing both `curl` and `/api/save`. **CONTRIBUTING Hazard #7 — written by §DX-02l itself in `91d3650` — now contains the sentence *"verifying §DX-02k needed raw `curl`"* on the same line as `POST /api/save`,** so the gate reads a historical account of the defect as an instruction to commit it. Proved pre-existing: the test fails at HEAD with a clean tree (stash-verified, `shasum -c` OK), so the §DX-02l ship record's *764 passed / 4 failed* predates its own last doc edit. **This makes the standing baseline FIVE reds, not four**, until it is fixed. **Fix shape — a design call, which is why it is a row and not a detour:** either narrow the assertion to an actual *instruction* shape (a fenced command line / a line starting with `curl`, not a sentence mentioning both tokens), or reword Hazard #7 so the two tokens never share a line. - [x] **§DX-02k — the argless `save()` was not a stray test call: it was the server's own per-write path, and it stamped a 5.4 MB snapshot on every PUT ✅ SHIPPED 2026-08-03 `2ead185`.** The premise held — `save(outputPath)` fell back to `getStampedName()` and left dated files behind — but **both of the row's framings were wrong, and the measurement is what showed it.** **(1) The destination is the process CWD, not "next to the module."** `getStampedName()` returns a **bare filename**, and `fs.writeFileSync` resolves a bare name against `process.cwd()`. Proved by loading the repo's HTML from a scratch directory: the snapshot landed in the scratch directory. It read as "the repo root" only because that is where the server runs — a script run from anywhere else littered *there*, silently. **(2) The argless callers were not scripts. The SERVER was.** `saveAndRestart` and `saveAndVerify` — the persist step behind **every** successful PUT/POST/DELETE — ran `WBAPI.save()` argless, then `copyFileSync(snapshot, GAME_FILE)`, and **never removed the snapshot**. Two more argless sites sat in the batch endpoints. So the row's own proposed fix, *"make the argless form server-only,"* would have left the actual litter source untouched. And the snapshot was never a backup of the pre-write state — **it holds the NEW text**; its only job was to be the byte source of the copy, which makes it pure redundancy the moment the copy lands. **The check the row asked for came back the other way, too:** `archive-snapshots.sh` / `watch-snapshots.sh` / `monitor-snapshots.py` do depend on the stamped *name*, but `docs/notes/docs-dev-environment.md` documents their input as a **deliberate `cp`** — so the per-write stamping was not feeding a feature, it was drowning one: a curated session history turned into per-keystroke noise (patch chain last advanced **2026-07-09**, no watcher running, **6 orphans / ~32 MB** in the root). **Shipped:** `save(dest)` writes exactly where told and **refuses with no argument**, naming the alternative in the error · new **`WBAPI.saveStamped([dir])`** — the deliberate dated backup, landing **beside the source file** (`POST /api/save`, `wbapi save`, the audit-fix + junction-nuke endpoints; the last four also had the bare-name CWD bug) · new server-only **`saveGameFile()`** — temp beside the game file + **atomic rename**, so nothing is left to sweep *and* a reader can never catch a half-written game file; on failure the temp is kept and its path returned. **Evidence:** the CWD claim proved by a scratch-directory probe **before** any edit; **the pre-fix test run demonstrated the bug on itself** — stashing the fix and re-running dropped **two more 5.4 MB snapshots into the repo root**, which is the whole defect in one observation; new `dx02k-save-destination.test.js` **6/6**, of which **5 fail on the stashed pre-fix tree** (restored, `shasum -c` OK — the passer is the `save(dest)` round trip, already true); live server round trip = **3 successful writes** (`act=1` idempotent, `act=2`, `act=1` back), each verified on disk by grep and through `GET`, ending at the **original shasum** with **0 new snapshots and 0 temp files**; `POST /api/save` still returns a dated backup beside the game file, so the archive surface is intact; `check:walk` **15/15 exit 0**; full Playwright **756 passed / 4 failed** = the documented `worldbuilder-crud-arrays` four (+6 new tests over the 750 baseline), with `multiplayer-presence:171` **flaky, retried green** — a first run showed it red on both attempts and a second full run reproduced the documented baseline exactly, so it is the known flake, not a regression; root swept to **one** `roll2hit-v3*.html`, and two full suite runs added none back. **The durable half is the inverse assertion in the test: no shipped code may call `WBAPI.save()` with no destination.** **The lesson: "did it persist?" is only half of a write path's acceptance test — the other half is "and nowhere else."** A stray write throws nothing, changes no behaviour, and is found only by looking at the directory. Docs: **CONTRIBUTING Hazard #7**, `index.md` (Version Snapshots + `wbapi-core.js` persist surfaces), `docs/notes/docs-dev-environment.md`, `docs/api/api-user-guide.md` (which described `POST /api/save` as how writes reach disk — they already did), and annotations on the three historical notes that still traced the old stamped path (`lab-report-wbapi-architecture.md` §4.2, `data-code-migration-into-cells.md`, `cell-resume-prompts.md`). *(Original row: `save(outputPath)` falls back to `this.getStampedName()`, which writes a dated `roll2hit-v3-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.html` snapshot **next to the module — the repo root**. That is right for the server's autosave, but any test or one-shot script calling `save()` argless leaves a multi-MB file behind on every run; two such snapshots are sitting in the root right now from earlier sessions, invisible because the pattern is gitignored. `dx02h-terrain-roster-write.test.js` was fixed to pass `save(tmp)` explicitly. Decide: have `save()` refuse when the destination would be the repo root outside a server context, or add a `saveTo()` and make the argless form server-only; either way sweep the existing snapshots. **Risk:** low, but check `archive-snapshots.sh` / `watch-snapshots.sh` first — one of them may depend on the stamped-name behaviour.)*

- [x] **§DX-02l — the dated-backup surface had no `./api.sh` wrapper, and the sweep it wanted would have destroyed the history it exists to keep ✅ SHIPPED 2026-08-03 `91d3650`.** The premise held exactly as filed: `./api.sh save` answered `✗ Unknown command "save"`, `api/wb.js` held **0** occurrences of `save`/`snapshots`, and three lines of the *author-facing* guide (`api-user-guide.md` §17.13 and both worked-example workflows) told authors to reach the surface with `curl -s -XPOST …/api/save | jq` — the golden rule broken in the docs that teach it. **Shipped API-first, endpoint before wrapper (prompt.md §2.5):** `GET /api/snapshots` (the dir, per-file size/mtime, total, and whether the patch chain already holds it) and `DELETE /api/snapshots` (nonce-guarded like every other destructive route), then `./api.sh save` and `./api.sh snapshots [--sweep] [--force]`. `snapshot` had to be added to the nonce endpoint's `validTypes` — it is the one type with **no collection behind it**, since the sweep destroys files, not entries, so the key resolution is skipped rather than run against `undefined`. **The row's framing of the sweep was the thing that changed on contact.** It called the disposal *"a `rm` a human has to remember"* — but `archive-snapshots.sh` **already disposes of them**, and it does so by diffing each snapshot into a `milepoints/patches` delta and *then* `rm`-ing the file. So a blunt sweep is not a chore automated, it is **the patch chain's input deleted before it is read**: an unarchived snapshot is the only copy of that state. `--sweep` therefore deletes only what the chain already holds (`<stem>.patch` present, or named by `_last.name`) and **names `./archive-snapshots.sh` in the skip reason**; `--force` is the deliberate discard. **Evidence:** live round trip on the real server before any test — `./api.sh save` → 5.2 MB backup beside the game file → `snapshots` listed it `unarchived` → `--sweep` **kept it** and said why → `--sweep --force` freed it, with `roll2hit-v3.html` at its **original shasum** and the root back to one file; new `dx02l-save-snapshots-cli.test.js` **7/7**, and **all 7 fail on the stashed pre-fix tree** (restored, `shasum -c` OK — nothing here is vacuous); `check:walk` **15/15 exit 0**; full Playwright **764 passed / 4 failed** = the documented `worldbuilder-crud-arrays` four, **0 flaky**. **No HTML shipped and no §7½ — authoring surface only; nothing a player sees changed.** **The durable half is what the sweep is allowed to name:** a decoy suite (`roll2hit-v3-notes.html`, `-2026.html`, `-20260709.html`, `-20260709-0341.html`, `.htm`, `.html.bak`) survives a **forced** sweep beside the game file, because only an exact `-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.html` stamp is reachable — the stamp is the entire guard between *delete the backups* and *delete the game*. The test also pins the row's own lesson: **no author-facing doc may reach `/api/save` with `curl`.** **The lesson: an endpoint whose only documented client is `curl` is not a finished write path — the wrapper is what makes it real, and "it has no wrapper" is usually visible in the docs before it is visible in the CLI.** Docs: `docs/api/api-user-guide.md` (§17.13 rewritten + both workflows + the endpoint card), `API-README.md` (new *Dated backups* section + 3 mapping rows), `wbapi-help.md`, `docs/notes/docs-dev-environment.md`, `index.md`, `prompt.md` §3 + §9, **CONTRIBUTING Hazard #7** (which now carries the reporting half: the directory is gitignored, so `./api.sh snapshots` is the only thing that will ever tell you what is in it), and `./api.sh help` gained a *Persistence* block under SERVER LIFECYCLE saying plainly that you do **not** need `save` after a write. *(Original row: )* Verifying that the dated-backup surface still worked needed a raw `curl -X POST http://localhost:1367/api/save`, because `./api.sh save` answers `✗ Unknown command "save"`. prompt.md §3's golden rule is that authoring never falls back to raw `curl` — *"if `./api.sh` lacks a command you need, add the endpoint + a named `./api.sh` wrapper"* — and here the endpoint exists while the wrapper does not, which is the same gap read from the other end. Small: an `api/wb.js` command that POSTs `/api/save` and prints the `backup` / `primary` paths. Worth doing together with a `./api.sh snapshots` (list/sweep the root's dated files) now that they are produced only on request — the sweep is currently a `rm` a human has to remember. **Risk:** trivial; read-modify of the CLI dispatch table only, no game-file writes.

### §AUDIT-03 — Quest-data appended-field rot (NEW 2026-07-28, surfaced by §VM-01-G3)

> §VM-01-G3 found that the bulk audit waves `a721254` ("80+ passText/failText/activateNode/desc/hint fields patched") and `ea02faf` ("wire npc field on all 985 quests") APPENDED fields to entries that already declared them — JS last-key-wins silently flipped authored values — and `710bb75` ("Fix 8 activateNode errors: SF→LCY, CQ→CDG, FR→AMS") remapped at least two dead codes to the WRONG target. G3 fixed the ~20 quests in its five arcs; these rows are the corpus-wide sweeps. All are data-only audits — grep/parse first, fix through `./api.sh` where expressible (⚠️ Hazard #1 for hand-edits).

  **Three defects found and fixed on the way (the row's own premises included):**
  1. **The accepted vocabulary was too narrow.** `_npcOk` (duplicated in two `wbapi-server.js` closures) and `advise` accepted only BIRKA_NPC + normalized `NODE_MAP` inline `npc` — so real, rendered speakers living in `NPC_DIALOGUES` (`jimmy`/`solvak`/`yva`/`rennau`/`kenickie`/`isolde_voss`/`benedikt_rasp`/`sandy_cat`) and the 20 `EB_NPC_DIALOGUE` quest-givers would all have advise-warned.   2. **`patchStringField` was not depth-aware — a silent no-op class.** The first batch reported `patched:196, errors:[]` but **6 writes never landed**: `editField('quest', id, 'npc', …)` matched the FIRST `npc:` token anywhere in the entry, which for `quest_wm_02/wm_03/tl_01/tl_03/vs_01/vs_02` is the **nested** `{ kind:'favor', npc:'…' }` inside `onComplete`. Fixed with a new `firstTopLevelMatch(body, re)` helper: a single string- and comment-aware pass builds a depth map, and only a match at brace depth 0 of the entry body can be chosen (comment-awareness per the §AUDIT-03f lesson). Re-ran the 6 → all correct, favor bits untouched. **Proof of zero collateral across the whole corpus: all 16 `kind:'favor', npc:` values byte-identical before vs after (git-diff extraction), and the game-file diff is exactly 196 insertions / 196 deletions.**

Note the scope limit before starting: `the XX node` is one phrasing — the sweep should first measure how many *other* phrasings carry a dead code (`at XX`, `north of XX`, a bare parenthesised code) before the gate's shape is fixed, exactly as §AUDIT-03m-FU had to widen from a LINE test to four hand-classified cues. **Risk:** low (prose + one scanner phase). **Verify:** the six strings changed and eyeballed live at `CDG`; a planted control string exits 1. **+1, 2026-08-12 (§DOC-02aa), and it is a new sub-shape: a live code naming the WRONG PLACE.** `hint:'Visit the City Inn to find the open page.',@11051` (`quest_ng_02`, Layer 50) is not a dead code at all — it is plain English, and it is wrong: the Entry 42 panel renders at `LHR` = **City Streets — Birka** (`if (node.code === 'LHR' && (S_story.ngPlusRun || 0) >= 1 && S_story.priorQuestMinusOne@34636`), while *The First Inn* is `TLL`. The error is **original**: the birth commit reads `node.code === 'CI'` and the same hint, and `CI` was `num:1, name:'city'`, never an inn. So the report, the home doc and the player-facing hint all inherited one author's wrong mental map of a node they had correctly transcribed. **This is the shape phase 7 cannot catch by design** — there is no code in the string to resolve — which is worth stating in the row rather than discovering later: the gate handles *dead codes in prose*, and a *wrong place-name in prose* needs a human or a `q.activateNode` → node-label cross-check. **+1 more shape, 2026-08-12 (§DOC-02ab): a retired node code preserved in an IDENTIFIER.** `returnedToCI: !!(S_story.visited && S_story.visited['LHR'] && S_story.level >= 5),@23661` — the property NAME still says `CI` while the value it reads was migrated to `LHR`. Not player-facing, so the cheapest member of the family, but invisible to **every** gate by construction: `check:legacycodes` scans `.md`, `check:noderegs` scans node *references* and a bare object key is neither, `check:anchors` scans docs. Worth one line in whatever phase 7 becomes — an object key that is a legacy code sitting beside a value that resolves is the exact shape that makes *"does this code exist?"* the wrong question.
> **EXTENDED 2026-08-12 (§DOC-02r) — the §WHODUNIT-01 resolution line is on a dead node.** `Ord the passenger is owed an apology@33628` (*"…the cook has declined to give"*) is the only place in 38,712 lines that closes the arc's moral beat, and it renders inside `node.code === 'SEN'`, which `LCY` suppresses (§AUDIT-03x). Not a dead *code* — a live, correct string on unreachable ground, which is the same invisibility with the opposite cause. Worth keeping in this row because the detector wanted for §AUDIT-03s (scan the **engine-string universe**, not just `.md` and not just comparison literals) is the one that would surface it.

This is the Hazard-#2 class in its data form — *a read of a real-but-wrong value never throws*. **The fix is two-sided:** (a) assign each of the 36 nodes a real act — most are late-arc historical content whose act is inferable from its neighbours, but a handful (the Chancery/Camelot restoration set) may be deliberately act-less and want an explicit sentinel instead, which is the one design call in the row; (b) add a gate — `check:invariants` is the natural home — failing on any `NODE_MAP` entry whose `act` is not an integer in `ACT_NAMES`' index range, since **no existing gate can see this**: `check:noderegs` checks that node *references* resolve, never that a node's own scalar fields are well-formed. **Risk:** low for the gate, low-medium for (a) — `actNumber` feeds act-gated quest/CSS behaviour, so changing 36 nodes off their silent Act 1 could surface content that was never reachable. **Verify:** the gate exits 1 on a planted `act:NaN`; the badge eyeballed live at `CI` and `RON` per §7½.

- [ ] **§DX-02p — a level earned by PASSING a skill check delivers no level-up (found 2026-08-11 during §DOC-02e).** `_checkLevelUp()`@25671 reads like a predicate and is a **mutator**: it advances `S_story.level` immediately and pushes the new level onto `_levelUpQueue`. Every *benefit* of that level — the hit-die roll for max HP, the ASI at 4/6/8/12/14/16/19, the Fighter feature, the level-2/9/17 surge and indomitable charges — is delivered by `_showLevelUpModal`@25615 and its continue handler, and **the queue is the only channel between them**. Every drain in the file: `@7015` (skill-check **FAIL**, §XP-01 effort XP) · `@25187` `_storyEnemyFlees` · `@25300` battle victory · `@30080` `_grantExplorationXp` · `@38442` victory-overlay return · `@38676` modal chaining. **The skill-check PASS path is not among them** — `_resolveQuestUQF`'s pass branch@6989 runs `execBits`, credits the warrant, calls `storyRender`, and never checks the queue. **It is worse than deferral:** `_grantExplorationXp` opens with `_levelUpQueue = []`@30078 and re-runs `_checkLevelUp()`, which returns immediately because the level was already advanced — so **any step onto new ground discards the pending entry**. The level is kept; its rewards are gone. **The asymmetry is the tell:** the failing branch, written later by §XP-01, does it correctly three lines away — *failing* a Ceremonia Roll can open the modal, *passing* one cannot. **Blast radius: all 2,453 `skill_check` quests**, not one arc. **The 2026-05-26 §DESIGN-03 spec called for exactly this** (*"If `_levelUpQueue.length > 0`: show level-up modal immediately"*) and it was dropped in the §ARCH-01 migration — which is the argument for the spec→shipped delta table as a permanent instrument. **Needs no design call.** **Fix:** copy the fail branch's three lines into the pass branch. **Risk:** low. **Verify:** a Playwright pin on the *property* — cross an XP threshold on a passing skill check, assert the modal opened — never on the incident (*pin the property, never the incident*, §VM-01-G4c).
- [ ] **§AUDIT-03w — the courier guard quotes a 20-gold bribe the engine cannot accept (found 2026-08-11 during §DOC-02e).** `quest_courier_release` ships `onFail:[]` — the empty array — and a `failText` reading *"'Twenty gold or a writ from the Watch Commander.' He turns the log face-down."*`@21338`. §8 of the 2026-05-26 spec designed the transaction in detail (a `'bribe_available'` quest status, a *"Pay 20gp Bribe"* secondary button, an `onFail` callback offering it when `gold >= 20`); `git log -S "bribe_available"` returns **0 commits ever**. So the game **states a price and cannot be paid it**. **This is §AUDIT-03v's class exactly** — prose that names a transaction the engine never honours — and finding a second instance in two consecutive increments makes it a **pattern worth a detector rather than two hand-filed rows**: a player-facing string that names a specific gold amount as an offer, with no `cost`/`reward` bit or `sleepCost` exemption behind it. **Small design call, two options:** (a) implement it — the grammar has supported this since §VM-01-G4a: a `choice` on the fail branch with a `{kind:'cost', gold:20, refuse:'…'}` option, where `refuse` covers the can't-afford case under the shipped refuse-at-click contract; or (b) rewrite `failText` to refuse without naming a number. **Do not do neither.** **Risk:** low either way. **Verify:** (a) `./api.sh advise quest_courier_release` + a round-trip pin that 20gp leaves the purse exactly once; (b) grep the string is gone. **Consider closing §AUDIT-03v in the same increment** — same class, same decision shape. **⟶ FOURTH AND FIFTH INSTANCES, 2026-08-11 (§DOC-02h), and they WIDEN THE DETECTOR PAST GOLD.** Both in §CROWN-01 Amendment A (`c0c952b`). (iv) **The Leviathan iodine burn CHARGES for a benefit that has no reader.** `_nodeHookHcaLeviathan@33107` renders a button labelled *"⚡🧂 Burn Charged Iodine Salt at the water's edge (+5 ATK this fight)"* (or *"+3"* for plain); clicking it **splices the item out of the inventory** and sets `` `S_story.iodineBuffActive = true; S_story.iodineBuffBonus = _hasChL ? 5 : 3;@33131` ``. In 38,707 lines `iodineBuffActive` has **exactly one reader** — `` `const iodineBonus = st.iodineBuffActive@22249` ``, inside `_rollSkill`. **No combat code reads it.** So the player pays a crafted item for a stated combat bonus that does not exist — and the buff **leaks**, since nothing at HCA consumes it, so it is silently spent by whatever unrelated skill check comes next. So a player who passes a DC 10 INT/Arcana check is **permanently inside the inversion field**: both healing sites (the inventory potion Drink handler and the Brynn's-Loaf Eat handler) route through the `[Void Flux] Heal → Hurt` branch, whose arithmetic is `hp + heal - half - half` — a **net +0 or +1 HP** — for the rest of the run, with no surface anywhere telling the player why potions stopped working. **Fix, no design call:** make Act III match its five siblings, which all complete on a battle — either `completion:{ battles:['RAI'] }` (the node the whole chain targets) or write `voidFluxCleared` on the RAI victory. **The durable half, and it widens a proposed gate:** this is the **inverse** of the §DX-02n family. A gate that wants to catch both must check **both directions of the reader/writer census**, and the cheapest place to run it is over gate-leaf flag names in `QUEST_DB`, where every name is a literal. **§DOC-02n — 2nd instance of the read-only class:** `S_story.fishingBaitSatchel` is declared `false` with **2 readers and 0 writers**, so the bait-satchel discount can never be earned and the Yugurt Lake find DC is permanently `10 − LuckMod` rather than the 8 the engine is written to offer. Confirms the §DX-02u finding that a `check:deadconsts` scoped to unread fields walks straight past a read-only field — the gate must census readers and writers **separately** and fail on either being zero.

- [ ] **§DESIGN-04 — nothing in the live game answers *"where do I find monster X?"* (found 2026-08-11 during §DOC-02c; 🟡 DESIGN CALL).** The 2026-05-21 battleground report was written to eliminate the "lost in a field" failure mode, and its instrument was `HUNTING_GROUNDS` — a bijective terrain→node table making the question an O(1) lookup. **§TIMELESS-01 (`7952752`, 2026-06-26) deleted it and nothing replaced it.** Measured at HEAD: no bestiary locator, no terrain index, no per-monster habitat surface — **398 monsters across 111 terrains and 416 nodes**, with the only route from "I need a wolf" to "I am fighting a wolf" being to walk until the seeded stream rolls one. By the original report's own criteria the failure mode it named is currently unaddressed. **This is a design call, not a defect**, because the modern game may legitimately answer the question a different way: quest `activateNode` puts the player where the content is, and the Warrant's Board (§BOARD-01) is already the social discovery surface. **The three options to put to the user:** (1) DECIDED-STAY — arrival-driven content is the answer and no locator is wanted; (2) a read-only **bestiary** surface listing, per monster, the terrains it appears in (data already exists — `WORLD_DB[t].monsters` inverted) with no navigation affordance; (3) route it through the Board as a bounty that names its terrain. **Do not build before the call.** Note the invariant fence on any option: a locator may *inform* movement but may never shortcut it (invariant #3, `` `no jump travel. checkpointNode@26048` ``).

- [ ] **§AUDIT-03ac — the Codex Core "Destroy" branch advertises a curse penalty, writes an undeclared field with zero readers, and shadows the real scoring function (found 2026-08-12 during §DOC-02p). NO DESIGN CALL.** `⚡ Destroy the housing — STR Ceremonia Roll DC 15@31825` labels the button *"(bypass Auros, +curseScore)"*; passing it runs `S_story.curseScore = (S_story.curseScore || 0) + 5;` and prints *"⚠ You broke something that could not be rebuilt. [curseScore +5]"*. **`function _curseScore() {@28191` recomputes the score from `_EB_CODES` on every call and never reads that field.** `S_story.curseScore` has **three occurrences in 38,712 lines** — the button label, its own self-referencing write, and the message string — **zero readers**, and it is **not declared in `_S_DEFAULTS()`**, so it is also an undeclared persisted field (§STATE-INIT class: the seed literal is supposed to be the single source of truth for new state). The advertised penalty for the game's sharpest moral shortcut — destroying the housing rather than confronting Commander Auros — costs the player nothing at all. **This is the §AUDIT-03v/w cluster's 9th instance and its worst shape:** the previous eight promise a mechanic that does not exist, so a grep finds nothing and the reader knows. This one names a mechanic that **does** exist, under its real identifier, and writes into a shadow of it — a reader greps `curseScore`, finds a writer, a reader and a player-facing label, and concludes the loop is closed. ***The detector this argues for is narrower and cheaper than the cluster's usual one: a persisted field whose name differs from a live function's by one leading underscore, with writers but no readers.*** **Fix (two lines, no call):** either delete the field and have the Destroy branch record its penalty through a term `_curseScore()` actually sums, or make `_curseScore()` add `S_story.curseScore` — the second is the smaller change and preserves the authored intent, but note it interacts with **§ENDING-01**, since it moves the score in the wrong direction (up), away from the endings that are already unreachable.

- [ ] **§EPIC-04 — the engine states two incompatible counts of the same in-fiction document, on two reachable surfaces, and has since the earliest surviving build (found 2026-08-12 during §DOC-02p). SMALL DESIGN CALL: which count is canon.** Warlord Mordus's negotiation line says the Void Shaman Kazrath's journal `mentions Birka. Twice.@26496` (*"You're right to press. Find out what he knows and we'll both pay better."*); Froberger's Journal Entry 26 says it `mentions Birka forty times.@27210` (*"The Master says. The Master believes."*). **Both strings are present verbatim at `32c10c5`, so this was born contradictory** — it is not drift, and no rename or migration is involved. **Both surfaces are reachable:** `negotiateLine` is read at three sites in the negotiation panel, and Entry 26 sits on `TRD`, a primary node in its cell, so `function storyCheckJournal(node) {@30209` will deliver it. The detail is plot-bearing on both ends — the count is the evidence for how deeply Birka is implicated in the Void, which is the through-line into the Auros reveal. The fix is one string; the call is whether the intended reading is *"two references, worth pressing for"* (Mordus's framing, a lead) or *"forty references, an obsession"* (Froberger's framing, a confession) — they characterise Kazrath differently, so this is a writing decision, not a typo. Found by reading a lab report that quotes **both numbers correctly, in two different sections**, which is what surfaced the disagreement: neither surface is wrong about itself.

### §DOC-02 — Lab-report verification program (NEW 2026-08-11)

> **Premise (user directive 2026-08-11):** the **107** files in `lab-reports/` are the project's design record, and most were written *before* the thing they describe shipped. They are HISTORY docs (`scripts/legacy-codes.js`) — never rewritten to hide what was believed at the time — but a spec that was never checked against the code reads exactly like a spec that was. The program: **take the oldest report by mtime, re-measure every claim against `roll2hit-v3.html`, rewrite it short and IEEE-shaped** (abstract · method · as-built inventory with `symbol@line` anchors · spec→shipped delta table · risk-register outcome · defects → BACKLOG rows), and file everything it finds. **The house rules that govern this work:** claims that did not ship are marked **NOT SHIPPED** and *kept*, never deleted (a silently removed claim reads as one that held); never read a node code off a doc table (§AUDIT-03m); and annotation without verification launders a wrong claim into a confident-looking live one (§AUDIT-03m-FU). **Ordering note (corrected 2026-08-11 by §DOC-02b — re-measured, the §DOC-02a figures were wrong):** the directory holds **107** `.md` files, not 109 (`git ls-files lab-reports/ | wc -l`; six were deleted by `120d617`). **44** of them shared one mtime (`2026-06-09 11:06:54`, a bulk copy) when the program opened — so "oldest" within that block is resolved alphabetically — and there are **45 distinct mtimes** in all. Each verified report gets a fresh mtime and leaves the block, so the block shrinks by one per increment (43 after §DOC-02a, 42 after §DOC-02b); **re-derive the ordering from `stat`, never from this note's arithmetic.**

The predictor is not whether a passage cites code but whether the author could **copy** it. **An eighth, and it is a gate hazard rather than a method: an anchor whose text is not a LITERAL substring of the line it points at is DEAD even when the line is perfectly alive.** §DOC-02f found **5 such anchors left by §DOC-02e** plus 1 of its own, and none of the six symbols had moved — all six lines existed, unchanged, at the cached number. The three ways to mint one, written here **without their `@line` suffixes so this row does not itself mint three more** — a counterexample inside backticks *is* an anchor to the gate, which is how §DOC-02f briefly re-broke it: **markdown table pipe-escaping** (an anchor reading `q.retryGateDays \|\| 1`, where `\|` is the table escape and the source says `||`), an **ellipsis** standing in for elided code (`checkLevelUp: () => { … _checkLevelUp(); }`), and **whitespace normalisation** (an anchor reading `const d20 = …` where the source has `const d20  =` with two spaces). The fix is always to shorten the anchor to the shortest unambiguous *verbatim* fragment — `` `q.retryGateDays@6811` ``, `` `checkLevelUp: () =>@22348` `` — never to widen it into a pretty quotation. **Related and worth stating plainly: §DOC-02e recorded `check:walk` 16/16 green while carrying those 5 dead anchors**, because the run hit the known harness detach artifact and never reached gate 15. *When the detach artifact fires, the gates that did not run are not green — re-run them individually before recording a result.* **Scope one report per increment** — §DOC-02a produced 2 audit rows + 2 doc corrections, §DOC-02b 1 defect row + 1 ordering correction, and §DOC-02c 2 defect rows, all from a single report each. **A fourth accelerator, added by §DOC-02c and now mandatory for any report with dead symbols:** run `git log -S "<symbol>" -- roll2hit-v3.html` on every symbol the census marks dead. It costs one command per symbol and separates **RETIRED** (shipped, later removed — the report was true when written) from **NOT SHIPPED** (never existed under that name — the report was written from intent, not from the file). §DOC-02c's headline finding came from exactly this: `stalkModal` and two of its DOM ids return **0 commits ever**, while the feature they describe shipped three days later under different names. *A report cannot make this distinction about itself; only history can.* **A fifth accelerator, added by §DOC-02d:** when a report names a character two ways, `grep` **both** names in the engine before writing the delta table — the split is usually still there as two keys, and it is the highest-value finding a content report can yield (§AUDIT-03n cost a whole row to repair one). **Three accelerators, now proven three times:** (1) the arc's *maintained* home doc (`story.md`/`world.md`) is usually already correct and annotated, so the lab report's job is the **delta table**, not a second copy of it; (2) the fastest first measurement is always `grep -c` on every key the report claims to have added — a missing entry is a delta, a present entry still needs its *fields* compared; and (3) **for any report that enumerates symbols, batch the whole name list through one `grep -c` loop before reading a line of it** — §DOC-02b's 197-symbol census took one command and immediately partitioned the report into 180 live claims and 17 dead subsystems, which is the shape of the delta table. **One thing to watch for that §DOC-02b found and §DOC-02a did not:** a long report can **contradict itself**, and the tiebreak is mechanical — *believe the section that cites a line number.*

Fixes: (1) **`test.afterEach` sweep** — GET `/api/session/who` → POST `/api/session/end` for every local session id, so each test starts clean (guarded `try/catch` for the afterAll window when the server is already gone). (2) **Assert by pid, never by count** — the reload ghost-check was `who.sessions.filter(name==='Odys')).toHaveLength(1)` (a raw count a cross-test leak inflates); now captures `pid = MP.pid` (stable across resume, `pid = pidOf(sid)`) and asserts `who.sessions.filter(name==='Odys').map(s=>s.pid)` `toEqual([pid])` — a ghost surfaces a *second, different* pid under the name; a leak can inflate a count but never forge a pid. Verified: `multiplayer-presence` **7/7** in 6.9 s (server-independent; dev :1367 restarted after). Test-file-only; no product code touched.
